content.text:
Base directory for this skill: /Users/kenneth/Projects/JusPrin/.claude/skills/jusprin-release

# Making a JusPrin release

The release workflow, `.github/workflows/jusprin_release.yml`, builds the
release files from one commit and uploads them to a draft release on GitHub.
It refuses the commit without a new version, release notes, a guide check and
the Sentry secrets, and fails a platform whose debug files or page source
maps did not reach Sentry (see "Releasing" in `AGENTS.md`). It does not run the test suites, check the
server, check the translations or audit error handling. This skill covers
those too, in the order they have to happen.

## Kenneth decides these

Ask Kenneth, in plain words, and wait for his yes before each of these. A yes
covers that one action, not the next one.

- The version number, when he has not named it.
- The release notes' wording. Show him the file.
- Deploying the server.
- Which error-handling findings must be fixed before the release.
- Taking in commits that landed on `jusprin-dev` after the range was fixed.
- The Sentry values and read-only token for checking the draft.
- Spending API money on live AI checks. Say the cost.
- Pushing to `jusprin-dev`, and moving `main` forward.
- Starting the release workflow.
- Downloading the draft's files to this computer.
- Posting anything on GitHub, such as replies to issues.

**Never publish the draft.** Kenneth publishes it by hand on the Releases page.
Never force-push `main`.

## When something has to be fixed

A fix for anything a step finds is its own commit on `jusprin-dev`, never
part of the release commit. Make it in a worktree of its own, on a branch
from `origin/jusprin-dev`, not in your release worktree. Pushing it needs
Kenneth's yes. Once it is on `origin/jusprin-dev`:

- **Before section 8 landed the release commit:** commit your release edits
  on your branch, rebase onto `origin/jusprin-dev`, and write down that
  commit as the new end of the range. Then redo step 1.4 and sections 2 to 7
  for the whole range. A fix can need a line in the notes, a translation, or
  a change to a test or the guide.
- **After it landed (a problem found in section 9 or 10):** the version is
  not released yet, so keep it. The new end of the range is the fix's commit
  on `origin/jusprin-dev`. Redo step 1.4 and sections 2 to 7 on a branch
  from it, land what changed as in section 8, move `main` to the new release
  commit, and start the workflow again (section 9). A new run for the same
  version replaces the draft's files and text.

If a step fails and you cannot tell why, stop and tell Kenneth with the
output. Do not skip the step.

## Where each platform is tested

Every release is tested on all three platforms, twice: the test suites in
section 5, and the draft's own files in section 10. A platform that was not
tested blocks the release; it is not a line in the report.

- **macOS:** this computer.
- **Windows and Linux:** two test VMs in Google Cloud. How to reach each one,
  start it, copy code to it, build and run the app there is in
  `<main checkout>/.claude/vm-harness/windows/README.md` and
  `<main checkout>/.claude/vm-harness/linux/README.md`. That folder lives
  only on this computer, not in the repository. Use the Google Cloud account
  your instructions name for `gcloud`. If a VM is stopped, start it, and
  stop it again when you are done with it.

If a VM cannot be reached or that folder is missing, stop and tell Kenneth.

## 1. Set up

1. Check that the main checkout (the folder that holds `jusprin-dev`, not a
   worktree) has nothing that would be left out of the release:

   ```bash
   git -C <main checkout> fetch origin
   git -C <main checkout> status --porcelain -uno
   git -C <main checkout> log --oneline origin/jusprin-dev..jusprin-dev
   ```

   Both must print nothing. A changed file or a commit that is not on GitHub
   is work someone may expect in the release. Stop, list each one for
   Kenneth, and wait until he has pushed it or said to leave it out. Do not
   push, commit or discard it yourself. Untracked files do not block: they
   are working docs Kenneth keeps there on purpose.
2. Find the last release: `git tag --list 'jusprin/v*' --sort=-v:refname | head -1`.
   Write down the commit `origin/jusprin-dev` points to now
   (`git rev-parse origin/jusprin-dev`). The range is the last release's tag
   to that commit, and every later step checks that range. Section 8 checks
   whether `jusprin-dev` moved since.
3. Settle the version now: Kenneth's, or ask him when he has not named one.
   Make your own worktree at that commit, under `<repo>/.claude/worktrees/`,
   on a branch named `claude/release-<version>`. Never name it
   `jusprin-release/...`: pushing a branch with that name starts an unsigned
   release build. If that branch name is taken, add a suffix.
4. Read every commit in the range: `git log --format='%h %s%n%b' <range>`.
   Note what a person would notice, and the GitHub issues each change fixes.

## 2. Version and release notes

1. Set `kVersion` in `src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/Updates/Version.hpp`. It must be
   above every released JusPrin version.
2. Write `src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/Packaging/release-notes/<version>.md`. The
   draft's text is this file, and each run of the release workflow writes it
   again. Once the release is published, an older app that offers the update
   shows that text under "Release notes" in Preferences › Updates. Follow the
   shape of the previous release's file. Write for a person who prints, not for
   a developer. Check every on-screen label you quote against the source
   (`git grep`), and leave out anything you have not checked.
3. A change that sends anything new from the person's computer, such as a new
   message to our server, goes in the notes and says what it holds.

## 3. Server readiness

The app calls JusPrin's server at `https://jusprinv2.obico.io`. Every address
the release calls must already be deployed there.

Many addresses are joined from pieces, so no single search finds them all.
List them from the code that builds them:

```bash
git grep -n -E '"/(ent|o|accounts|jusprin)/|"/models"|ask_server\("' -- src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin ':!*test*'
```

Read each hit and write out the full path. For example, `ask_server("code/confirm", …)`
in `Agent/CloudAccount.cpp` is `/ent/jusprin/v2/auth/code/confirm`, and the
model list is the gateway's address with its last part replaced by `/models`.
Leave off any query string. Check full paths only, never a bare prefix such
as `/ent/jusprin/v2/auth/`.

GET each one: `curl -s -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code}\n' https://jusprinv2.obico.io<path>`.
First GET a path that cannot exist, such as `/ent/jusprin/v2/no-such-address`.
It must answer 404. If it answers anything else, the check cannot tell
addresses apart: in maintenance mode the server answers 200 with the same
page for every path. Stop and tell Kenneth.

Then, for each address, an answer of 200, 3xx, 400, 401, 403, 405 or 426
means it is there. A 5xx means the server is failing: stop and tell Kenneth.
A 404 means it is not deployed. For a 404, find the server change in the tsd-enterprise
repository (`web_ent/jusprin/v2/urls.py` on `master`), tell Kenneth what is
missing, and wait until it is deployed. Also tell him about any other server
behavior a change in the range relies on, such as a new error code.

## 4. Error-handling audit

Run the `error-handling` skill on the range. When the release relies on
server changes, also audit the tsd-enterprise commits under `web_ent/jusprin/`
on `master` since the previous release tag's date (that repository has no
release tags).

Report the findings to Kenneth and wait. He says which ones must be fixed
before the release. Fixes follow "When something has to be fixed" above.

## 5. Tests

Build in your worktree, in Release, following "Building on a shared machine"
in `AGENTS.md`: check the load first, use `-j4`, choose every target before
you start. A new worktree has no dependencies of its own, so configure it
against the main checkout's. Use CMake.app's cmake (Homebrew's fails to find
Eigen3), absolute paths (the shell's folder can change between commands), and
put node on `PATH` for the pages:

```bash
export PATH=/Applications/CMake.app/Contents/bin:<node bin folder>:$PATH
cmake -S <worktree> -B <worktree>/build/arm64 -G "Ninja Multi-Config" -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Release \
  -DCMAKE_OSX_ARCHITECTURES=arm64 -DCMAKE_OSX_DEPLOYMENT_TARGET=15.0 \
  -DCMAKE_PREFIX_PATH=<main checkout>/deps/build/arm64/OrcaSlicer_dep/usr/local \
  -DSLIC3R_GUI=ON -DSLIC3R_STATIC=ON -DSLIC3R_PCH=ON -DBUILD_TESTS=ON \
  -DCMAKE_AR=/opt/homebrew/opt/llvm/bin/llvm-ar -DCMAKE_RANLIB=/opt/homebrew/opt/llvm/bin/llvm-ranlib
cmake --build <worktree>/build/arm64 --config Release \
  --target tests/all jusprin_web jusprin_catalogs -- -j4
ctest --test-dir <worktree>/build/arm64/tests -C Release --output-on-failure -LE RequiresApp
```

`tests/all` builds every test program: OrcaSlicer's suites, JusPrin's
(`agent_bridge_tests`, `jusprin_tests`, `jusprin_update_tests`,
`jusprin_profile_tests`, `shell_theme_tests`, `jusprin_fake_bambu_tests` and
the rest), `tool_call_check` and `shell_integration_harness`, which the guide
check uses. `ctest` runs every suite registered with it. `agent_live_tests`
is built but never registered, because each run costs API money. Also run
`npm test` in `src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/AgentUI` and in
`src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/HomeUI`.

- Windows and Linux: the release workflow neither builds nor runs the tests,
  so nothing else shows they even compile there. Build and run them on each:
  `build_win.bat -s --run-tests` on Windows, and on Linux `./build_linux.sh -st`
  then `ctest --test-dir build/tests -C Release --output-on-failure` (keep
  the `RequiresApp` tests there: they run only on Linux). Run them on the
  Windows and Linux VMs ("Where each platform is tested"), from a checkout
  of the end of the range.
- When the range changes text the model reads (prompts, skills, tool
  descriptions, tool results, how history is sent), run the live prompt suite
  (`tests/project_prompt/README.md`, and `tests/printer_prompt` when printer
  chats changed). Its `claude-cli` backend costs no API money. The README
  also asks for a small paid run on the app's default model before a release.
  Propose it to Kenneth with its cost, and run it only after his yes.

Report each failure with its output. To tell whether the range caused it,
run the same test on a build of the last release's tag. A failure there too
is older than this release: report it as such and let Kenneth decide. A
failure the range caused is a bug: fix it as "When something has to be
fixed" says, never skip the step.

## 6. Translations

These come after the audit and the tests, since a fix from either can add a
sentence.

1. Run `python3 src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/Localization/update_catalogs.py`. It
   needs GNU gettext and `npm ci` in `src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/AgentUI`. If it
   changes any catalog, those changes go into the release commit.
2. Translate every new entry in every language, as
   `src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/Localization/README.md` says. Those catalogs are
   JusPrin's own, in `Localization/native/` and `Localization/pages/`. Never
   edit upstream's `localization/i18n/` and never run `run_gettext`. From
   "Localization & translations" in `AGENTS.md` and the `orca-translations`
   skill, take only the editing rules and the glossary.
3. `npx vitest run src/catalogs.test.ts` in `AgentUI` must pass: it fails
   while an entry is untranslated or a translation lost a placeholder.
4. Rebuild `jusprin_web` and `jusprin_catalogs` so the guide check in step 7
   runs on the new catalogs.
5. Count the entries marked `# Needs human review` in
   `Localization/native/*.po` and `Localization/pages/*.po`. Tell Kenneth the
   count, so he can decide whether someone should read a language.

These steps cannot find a sentence nobody marked for translation. While
reading the range, look for text a person reads that is not marked.

## 7. Guide check

Follow "Before a release" in `docs/guide/README.md`, on the build from step 5
with the new version already in `Version.hpp`.

1. Tell Kenneth first: the command drives the app on this computer's screen
   for about a minute a page, so nobody should use the computer meanwhile.
2. Look through `git log <range> -- src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin` for new screens or
   menu items no page mentions, and add them to the guide. Do this first: the
   check below cannot find them, and a page changed after it passes was not
   checked.
3. Run your worktree's copy, `<worktree>/scripts/check_guide.py --ask-ai`,
   with node on `PATH`. The script checks the tree it sits in, so the main
   checkout's copy would check the wrong code. Fix what it reports until it
   passes. It then writes the version to `docs/guide/checked-version.txt`. If
   you change any page afterwards, run it again.

## 8. Commit and land

1. Commit on your branch: `Version.hpp`, the release notes, the catalogs in
   `Localization/native/` and `Localization/pages/`, everything the guide
   check changed in `docs/guide/` (pages, `pictures/`, `checked-version.txt`)
   and the guide skills it rebuilt in `AgentUI/src/skills/guide-*/`. Make
   sure no temporary working docs, logs or screenshots outside
   `docs/guide/pictures/` are in it.
2. Run `git fetch origin` and compare `origin/jusprin-dev` with the latest
   end of the range you wrote down. If it moved, those new commits have had none of the
   checks above. List them for Kenneth and wait for his answer. With his yes,
   rebase onto `origin/jusprin-dev` and redo step 1.4 and sections 2 to 7 for
   the whole range. If he says no, stop: the release waits until he decides, because
   your branch cannot reach `jusprin-dev` without those commits.
3. With Kenneth's yes, land it on `jusprin-dev` without a merge commit:
   `git push origin HEAD:jusprin-dev`. Then bring the main checkout along:
   `git -C <main checkout> pull --ff-only`. If that pull is refused, someone
   committed in the main checkout meanwhile: stop and tell Kenneth, and do not
   change the main checkout. Write down your commit
   (`git rev-parse HEAD`). This is the release commit.
4. With Kenneth's yes, move `main` to that exact commit:
   `git push origin <release commit>:main`. This only succeeds as a fast
   forward. If it is refused, stop and tell Kenneth. Never force it.

## 9. Start the release workflow

Only the release publisher may run it: the repository variable
`JUSPRIN_RELEASE_PUBLISHER`, or `kennethjiang` when that is unset. The `gh`
token on this computer may not be allowed to read the variable (`gh variable
list` can answer 403). Check that `gh api user -q .login` prints
`kennethjiang`. If the run's first job fails with "Only @<name> may make a
JusPrin release", tell Kenneth.

The workflow refuses to start without five Sentry secrets:
`JUSPRIN_SENTRY_DSN` (the project the app sends reports to), and
`SENTRY_AUTH_TOKEN`, `SENTRY_URL`, `SENTRY_ORG` and `SENTRY_PROJECT` (which
upload the debug files and page source maps that let Sentry name the
functions in a stack, with file and line). The `gh` token on this computer
cannot list secrets (`gh secret list` answers 403), so do not try. If the
run's first job fails on a missing secret, tell Kenneth which one. Only he
can add it.

With his yes:

```bash
gh workflow run jusprin_release.yml --ref main -f sign_macos=true
gh run list --workflow jusprin_release.yml --limit 3 --json databaseId,headSha,createdAt,event
```

Run the second command about 15 seconds after the first: a new run takes a
few seconds to appear. Take the `workflow_dispatch` run
created after you started it, and check that its `headSha` is the release
commit. Keep Mac signing on:
Homebrew refuses a Mac app that is not signed and notarised. Wait for the run
in the background (`gh run watch <databaseId>`). If its "Upload to the draft
release" job waits for an approval (the `release` environment can require
one), tell Kenneth. A failed run is a failure to report with its log, not a
reason to tick a skip box.

## 10. Test the draft

The draft holds the Windows installer and portable zip, the Mac disk image,
the Linux AppImage and `SHA256SUMS.txt`. These files are what people will get,
so test them, not a local build. Ask Kenneth before downloading them.

On each platform: the Mac disk image on this computer, and the Windows
installer and the AppImage on their VMs. Install over the previous release
and start the app. Check
that Preferences shows the new version. Kenneth signs in, or you use a test
account he names: never type a password yourself. Have one chat (it spends
that account's credits), slice, and
check each fix in the notes on the platform where it mattered (for example a
locale bug on Windows, where it always shows).

Check that Sentry can read this release's stacks, on the draft's own files.
Run both scripts from your release worktree on the Mac, for the Mac disk
image and for the Windows portable zip unpacked there (its `JusPrin/` folder
holds `OrcaSlicer.dll` and `resources`). Run the AppImage's part on the Linux
VM, in a checkout of the release commit with node and npx:
`--appimage-extract` only works on Linux.
Both scripts read `SENTRY_URL`, `SENTRY_ORG`, `SENTRY_PROJECT` and
`SENTRY_AUTH_TOKEN` from the environment. GitHub secrets cannot be read back,
so ask Kenneth for the values and for a token that can only read the
project. Set them in the shell for these commands only, and never write
them into a file.

- Run `src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/Packaging/sentry_debug_files.sh verify <file>`
  on the Mac app's `Contents/MacOS/OrcaSlicer` (it checks both
  architectures), Windows' `OrcaSlicer.dll` and the AppImage's
  `bin/orca-slicer` (`--appimage-extract` puts it under `squashfs-root`).
  Each must print "Sentry holds debug information".
- Run `src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/Packaging/sentry_page_maps.sh verify <folder>`
  from the release commit, with the folder that holds `jusprin/agent` and
  `jusprin/home` in each platform's app: the Mac app's `Contents/Resources`,
  the unpacked Windows zip's `JusPrin/resources`, the AppImage's `squashfs-root/resources`.
  Each must print "Sentry holds the agent page's source map" and the same
  for home.
- If an unexpected error happens while you test, send its report and open
  it in Sentry (the project `SENTRY_PROJECT` names, filtered by
  `release:"JusPrin <version> (OrcaSlicer <SoftFever_VERSION>)"`, the name
  `Updates::version_label()` gives, with `SoftFever_VERSION` from
  `version.inc`). The frames of the app's own code must show function names
  with file and line, not only addresses. The app has no way to cause one on
  purpose, and Help › Report a problem opens a GitHub issue, not a Sentry
  report. If none happens, say this check was not done; the two scripts
  above cover whether Sentry can read the stacks.

Before Kenneth publishes, check `gh workflow list --all | grep -i winget`.
`winget_updater.yml` is inherited from OrcaSlicer. It runs when a release is
published and submits the installer to winget as `SoftFever.OrcaSlicer`. It
must say `disabled_manually`. If it is enabled, tell Kenneth before he
publishes.

Tell Kenneth what was tested on which platform and what was not. He publishes.

## 11. After publishing

- Start the previous release on one computer and check that Preferences ›
  Updates offers the new version. The update check reads only published
  releases, so this is the first moment it can be checked.
- Reply to and close the GitHub issues the release fixes, with Kenneth's yes.
- Homebrew: if JusPrin's cask is in Homebrew/homebrew-cask
  (`brew info --cask jusprin` finds it), it needs a pull request there for
  the new version. Opening it is posting on GitHub, so it needs Kenneth's yes.
- Open the newest events in Sentry for the new release and check that a
  report's or crash's stack names the app's functions with file and line,
  and that a page error's frames name the page's source files
  (`HomeUI/src/...`, `AgentUI/src/...`). A stack of bare addresses or of
  `app:///home/index.html` positions means a platform's debug files or a
  page's map are missing: run `sentry_debug_files.sh verify` or
  `sentry_page_maps.sh verify` on that platform's released files.
- The next day, run the `jusprin-production-check` skill in the tsd-enterprise
  repository for new failures from the new version.
- Remove your worktree and branch.

50	The app's error reports used to go to JusPrin's server as five short text
51	fields, which passed them on to Sentry. They now go straight from the app
52	to Sentry through Sentry's own SDKs, and crashes are caught too. Kenneth:
53	"We want the Sentry server to capture as much info as possible so that we
54	can do production troubleshooting."
55	
56	What a report carries now
57	- The app uses sentry-native 0.17.5 (deps/Sentry) with the crashpad
58	  backend. Crashpad writes a crash's minidump from its own process,
59	  crashpad_handler, which ships beside the app on every platform. The SDK
60	  hands each envelope to OrcaSlicer's own HTTP client, which already knows
61	  the system's certificates and proxy.
62	- Nothing leaves without consent (the SDK's require_user_consent). With
63	  automatic reports on, reports and crashes go as they happen. With them
64	  off, only the one report the person chose to send goes; a crash stays on
65	  disk.
66	- Each event has what the SDK collects: the stack, the loaded modules, the
67	  machine, the recent steps (each page message's type and each tool call's
68	  outcome, never a payload), and this run's log file. It is filed by
69	  release, by what the app was doing and by the system, and grouped
70	  without the request ids that differ every time one failure happens.
71	- The stack is where the exception was thrown, not where the top handler
72	  reported it (Support/ThrowStack): the app's own __cxa_throw records
73	  each throw on macOS and Linux, and a vectored exception handler does it
74	  on Windows.

76	  replaced by "~", and fields are no longer cut to the old server's

82	- Each page builds its event with @sentry/browser 11.10.0 and hands it to
83	  the app in its report_error message; the page itself never reaches the
84	  network for this. The app sends it like its own reports.

86	  served from resources/jusprin by a scheme handler each web view
87	  registers (Support/PageScheme). WKWebView and WebKitGTK tell a file://

JusPrin 2 is a major upgrade. We rebuilt nearly everything: it is now built on OrcaSlicer 2.5.0, and every project has AI working beside it. The goal is the one JusPrin started with: make 3D printing simpler for hobbyists. You tell AI what you are printing and what went wrong. AI reads your file, your settings and your slice, changes the settings and slices again.

## What AI can do

Each project has an AI chat beside the 3D view. Ask in plain words, and AI works in the open project:

- Set up the printer, filament and print settings for the part you are printing.
- Open a model or project file, place objects on the plate, and lay out plates.
- Cut, split, merge and repair objects.
- Change print settings for you.
- Slice the plate and check the result, for example support printed inside a hole, or a part that starts in the air.
- Look at a photo of a failed print and suggest what to change.
- Run a filament calibration test (temperature, flow or pressure advance), read a photo of the printed test, and save the result as a new filament preset.

When you ask AI to print, it opens the usual send dialog. You choose the options and press Send. AI never starts a print.

When a slice has a problem, a marker on the 3D view shows it. Press Ask AI to have AI explain the problem and your options.

## Ways to use AI

- Sign up for a JusPrin account in the app. New accounts get free credits, and no card is needed.
- Use your own OpenAI, Anthropic or OpenRouter API key.
- Connect an AI app you already use: Claude Code, Codex, Claude Desktop, Cowork, Cursor or VS Code. It can then work with the project open in JusPrin.
- Or skip AI and just slice.

## Also new

- **Home screen.** Your projects and printers are on one screen. Each printer card shows the printer's status, and once the printer is connected, opens its own window.
- **Printers.** Add a printer and connect it by chatting with AI. You can connect Bambu Lab printers in LAN mode, and Klipper (Moonraker) and OctoPrint printers.
- **Saving.** Projects save themselves, so JusPrin never asks you to save or discard. File › Save (Cmd+S on a Mac, Ctrl+S on Windows and Linux) keeps a version you can go back to in File › Version history. Saving doesn't write over the .3mf file you opened. To get a .3mf file, use File › Export › Project 3MF (Cmd+Shift+S or Ctrl+Shift+S).
- **Opening files.** A file you open from Finder or File Explorer opens as a new project. A model dropped on the 3D view is added to the open project.
- **Check print.** Print › Check print shows a report of the slice beside the preview.
- **Print history.** Every sliced file you export or send to a printer is listed on Home's Print history, and you can print it again from there.
- **Classic view.** View › Switch to classic view shows OrcaSlicer's full interface. Press Back to JusPrin to return.
- **Updates.** JusPrin checks its GitHub releases for a new version once a day. You see the result in Preferences › Updates.
- **Reporting a problem.** Help › Report a problem opens a new GitHub issue in your browser, with the app's version and your system filled in.

## Upgrading from JusPrin 1.4

- **Installing.** On Windows, the installer replaces JusPrin 1. On a Mac, JusPrin 2 is also called JusPrin.app, so dragging it to Applications replaces JusPrin 1. On Linux, the AppImage is a new file, and JusPrin 1's AppImage stays where it is.
- **Your printers.** The first time JusPrin 2 starts, it offers to import your printers from JusPrin 1 or OrcaSlicer, with their filaments and print settings. You choose which printers to import. You can import later with Printer › Import printers from JusPrin 1 or Import printers from OrcaSlicer.
- **Your JusPrin 1 folder.** JusPrin 2 keeps its settings in a new folder. It only reads JusPrin 1's folder and never changes it. JusPrin 1's app settings, such as units and language, aren't imported.
- **Your account.** Your JusPrin 1 sign-in doesn't carry over. To use AI with a JusPrin account, sign up in JusPrin 2, even if you had an account in JusPrin 1. Chats from JusPrin 1 aren't imported.

## Downloads

- **Windows (64-bit):** the installer, or the portable .zip, which runs without installing.
- **Mac:** one disk image for Macs with Apple silicon and Intel Macs.
- **Linux (64-bit):** an AppImage, built on Ubuntu 24.04. Make the file executable, then run it.
- **SHA256SUMS.txt** lists each file's checksum.

Questions or problems: write to jusprin-support@obico.io, or use Help › Report a problem in the app.

#pragma once

#include "libslic3r_version.h"

#include <string>

namespace Slic3r::GUI::JusPrin::Updates {

// JusPrin's own version: what Preferences shows and what the update check
// compares with the version in each JusPrin release tag. It is separate
// from SoftFever_VERSION, OrcaSlicer's version, which this build keeps
// because 3MF projects, profile updates, the user_backup-v<version> folder
// and AppConfig's upgrade logic all read it.
inline constexpr char kVersion[] = "2.0.0";

// The version a problem report or a saved chat names: JusPrin's and the
// OrcaSlicer release it is built on, as "JusPrin 2.0.0 (OrcaSlicer 2.5.0)".
// Not SLIC3R_VERSION, which is OrcaSlicer's Bambu network-plugin
// compatibility number (02.08.01.55), not a release anyone can look up.
inline std::string version_label() { return std::string("JusPrin ") + kVersion + " (OrcaSlicer " + SoftFever_VERSION + ")"; }

// The User-Agent of every request JusPrin sends to its own server, so the
// server can tell JusPrin releases apart. Orca's Http sends
// "JusPrin/<SoftFever_VERSION>" by default, which names the OrcaSlicer
// release and is the same for every JusPrin release built on it.
inline std::string user_agent() { return std::string("JusPrin/") + kVersion + " OrcaSlicer/" + SoftFever_VERSION; }

} // namespace Slic3r::GUI::JusPrin::Updates

# JusPrin: Sentry's native SDK, which files JusPrin's error reports and
# catches crashes (src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/Support/SentryClient.cpp).
#
# The release zip, not the tag's archive: it carries crashpad and the other
# submodules. Crashpad writes a crash's minidump from its own process,
# crashpad_handler, which ships beside the app.
#
# The SDK sends nothing itself (SENTRY_TRANSPORT none): the app hands its
# events to OrcaSlicer's own HTTP client, which already knows the system's
# certificates and proxy on every platform. Crashpad uploads a crash from its
# handler with the system's own HTTP on macOS and Windows, and with curl on
# Linux, hence the curl dependency there.
set(_sentry_depends ${ZLIB_PKG})

=== 25c280af8d JusPrin 2: server text in the app's language
The pages the JusPrin 2 app opens (prices, billing, cancel, purchase done),
the account box, the sentences /ent/jusprin/v2/account sends for the app to
show, and the sign-in code email are now translated into the app's 22
languages besides English, the same set OrcaSlicer ships.

How the language is chosen (jusprin/v2/language.py, a middleware for
/ent/jusprin/v2/ only, after Django's LocaleMiddleware): a ?lang= on a link,
then a jusprin_language cookie, then Accept-Language, then English. The app
sends its own language in Accept-Language. Its sheet is a web view that sends
the computer's language instead, so web_link stores the app's language with
the link (or puts ?lang= on a guest link) and the opened page sets the cookie,
which keeps the language through sign-out and Chargebee and back.

Sentences are whole translatable units: no English fragments are joined, and
counts use plural forms. Sentences placed one after another go through a
translatable joiner, so Japanese and Chinese have no space after their full
stop. Dates use a format each language supplies: the full month name in the
form the language writes after a day, or numbers where the month name would
need an elided article (Italian, Catalan) or end in a dot that doubles the
full stop (Lithuanian). Prices use a translatable "$%(amount)s".

The catalogs are machine-translated and marked "# AI Translated". The
compiled .mo files are committed (a .gitignore exception), as Obico's are,
because the web image doesn't compile catalogs; test_language.py fails when
an entry is untranslated or a .mo is behind its .po. The README's "JusPrin
2's server text" section says how to update them.

Chargebee's checkout and receipts, Obico's own sign-in pages, and the plan
names Hobby and Workshop stay English.

=== bcd0fc94b0 JusPrin 2: report every failure a person cannot act on, and take the app's error reports
A failure the person can do nothing about is answered "Something went wrong
on our side" and goes to Sentry with everything known about it. A failure
they can act on keeps its own answer. Kenneth, 2026-11-16: "if the error is
something that user can do nothing about, just show the user a generic error
message and give user a way to report a problem. On the back end though, we
need to make sure we send as much info as possible to the Sentry server so
that we can do root cause analysis. And that's it, nothing else."

The AI gateway (/ent/jusprin/v2/messages and /responses):
- The provider refusing a request (any status but 200 and 413), failing or
  going quiet partway through a reply, being unreachable or too slow, and the
  server's own slots for large requests being full all reach the one handler
  at the top of the endpoint. Before, a 400 was passed off as a 502, a
  failure inside a reply was recorded as a completed reply, and an outage or
  a timeout got an answer of its own and reached no Sentry.
- A completed reply that cannot be kept afterwards, and a chat title the app
  did not encode as UTF-8, reach the same handler. Before, the first was
  caught where it happened and the second was read with its bad bytes
  replaced.
- The report carries the provider's status, request id and error text, and
  the request's user, chat, turn, kind, alias, model and outcome.
- None of these is recorded as a completed reply or kept as one.
- Answers of their own, in errors.EXPECTED: signed out, out of credits, app
  too old, too many turns a minute, chat too large for the provider, and the
  four refusals of a print report.

The Django views: a failure reaches Sentry through its Django integration.
The app is told the same sentence as JSON; a page in the app's sheet shows it
in the app's language.

Checkout and cancel: Chargebee refusing a checkout or a cancel is not the
person's to act on, so it goes up; "Checkout couldn't start" and "The plan
couldn't be cancelled" are gone. So does a checkout that comes back in any
state but succeeded or cancelled, one that bought neither a JusPrin 2 plan
nor a pack, and one that is another account's. A checkout the person
cancelled goes back to the prices, as before.

and passes it to the Sentry project named by JUSPRIN_V2_APP_SENTRY_DSN. That

input.content:
JusPrin 2.0.1 speaks your language, connects more printers from the printer chat, and fixes printers that could not be added in languages that write decimals with a comma.

## New

- **JusPrin in your language.** JusPrin's own screens, the AI chat and Home are translated into the 22 languages OrcaSlicer ships. JusPrin uses the language you chose in Preferences. Numbers follow it too, for example "0,4 mm" in German. The translations are machine-made, so some wording may read oddly. AI still answers in the language you write to it.
- **More printers connect from the printer chat.** The printer chat can now connect every connection type OrcaSlicer's printer settings offer, not only Klipper (Moonraker) and OctoPrint. This includes Elegoo Centauri Carbon and Centauri Carbon 2 printers (Elegoo Link). The chat cannot finish Repetier, UltiMaker, or PrusaLink with a user name and password, and tells you where to set those up instead. Obico, SimplyPrint and 3DPrinterOS still need their own sign-in.
- **Reporting errors.** When something goes wrong that you can't fix yourself, JusPrin shows one message, "Something went wrong on our side". You can see the whole report, then press Report to JusPrin team, or tick "From now on, report errors like this automatically". You can also turn this on or off in Preferences › Updates › Error reports. It is off until you turn it on.

## Fixed

- In languages that write decimals with a comma, such as German, French, Spanish, Portuguese and Russian, the add-printer form showed no nozzle sizes for most printers, so the printer could not be added. Bed sizes such as 233.5 mm were also read as 233 mm, and a 0.4 mm nozzle in an opened 3MF file was read as 0. This always happened on Windows.
- A calibration test started from one of your projects lost that project and its chat.
- A project could save itself again after sitting idle, with nothing changed.
- A file the AI chat refused to attach (too large, or a kind it can't read) stopped the project from saving until you removed it.
- If JusPrin couldn't write its settings file, signing in or saving an API key looked like it worked, and was lost when you quit. Preferences now says it couldn't be kept.
- Deleting your account now waits while AI is still replying in the main window.
- A chat whose account or API key was removed showed the wrong model in its greyed-out model picker. It now shows the model the chat ran on.
- When AI prepared a print, it could keep checking the slice it had just started, again and again, while the slice ran.

## What JusPrin now sends

- **When the app starts**, it tells JusPrin's server once that it started: a random number made on the first start, the app's version and the name of your operating system. Nothing in it names you, and no sign-in goes with it. It is not sent in stealth mode.
- **Error reports and crashes** go to JusPrin's error tracker (Sentry) only when you press Report to JusPrin team, or when you have turned on automatic reports. A report holds where in the app the error happened, your computer's system and the app's log for that run. A crash report also holds the state of the app when it crashed. With automatic reports off, a crash report stays on your computer.

## Downloads

- **Windows (64-bit):** the installer, or the portable .zip, which runs without installing.
- **Mac:** one disk image for Macs with Apple silicon and Intel Macs.
- **Linux (64-bit):** an AppImage, built on Ubuntu 24.04. Make the file executable, then run it.
- **SHA256SUMS.txt** lists each file's checksum.

Questions or problems: write to jusprin-support@obico.io, or use Help › Report a problem in the app.

# Windows GUI test VM (GCP) — working harness

Drives a wxWidgets + OpenGL desktop app on a GPU-less Windows VM in GCP,
headlessly: launch it, screenshot it, click it, verify the result.

Verified 2026-09-07 with OrcaSlicer 2.4.2 portable.

## The VM

    instance : jusprin-win-test
    project  : elegoo-backend
    zone     : us-central1-a
    machine  : n2-standard-8, Windows Server 2022, 100GB pd-balanced
    display  : virtual display device ENABLED (required, see below)
    login    : ssh as guitest with ~/.ssh/google_compute_engine

The external IP is ephemeral and CHANGES on every stop/start. Re-read it with:

    gcloud compute instances describe jusprin-win-test --zone=us-central1-a \
      --project=elegoo-backend \
      --format="value(networkInterfaces[0].accessConfigs[0].natIP)"

then update winssh.sh / winscp.sh.

## Four things that had to be solved

1. **OpenGL.** The app hard-requires OpenGL 3.2 (src/slic3r/GUI/OpenGLManager.cpp)
   and exits below it. Stock Windows software rendering reports 1.1. Fix: drop
   Mesa's `opengl32.dll` + `libgallium_wgl.dll` (from pal1000/mesa-dist-win) next
   to the .exe. Reports OpenGL 4.2 on plain CPU.

   Mesa then auto-picks its **d3d12** backend, because the GCE virtual display
   exposes "Microsoft Basic Render Driver" as a D3D12 device — and that path
   crashed on the first frame. run-app.cmd forces the CPU rasterizer with
   `GALLIUM_DRIVER=llvmpipe` and `LIBGL_ALWAYS_SOFTWARE=1`.

   Do NOT copy the whole Mesa .7z onto the VM: Windows Defender flags the archive
   as Trojan:Win32/Suschil!rfn and deletes it. Extract the two DLLs elsewhere and
   copy just those — Defender does not object to them, so no AV exclusion is
   needed. (The archive's sha256 matches GitHub's published release digest; the
   detection is a heuristic on the bundle, which also contains Vulkan layers,
   D3D12 compilers and media-foundation encoders we don't use.)

2. **A visible desktop.** A GUI app started from an SSH shell lands in a session
   with no desktop and screenshots come back black. autologon.ps1 creates a local
   admin `guitest` and sets Winlogon AutoAdminLogon so console session 1 is always
   live. Something in the GCE image clears those values after the boot that sets
   them, so startup.ps1 re-applies them on EVERY boot.

3. **Session isolation.** Display APIs, EnumWindows and Get-Process MainWindowTitle
   only see the CALLING session's window station. Run them over SSH and they
   silently report nothing — which reads as "the app has no window" when it does.
   Everything that touches the UI goes through `Invoke-InSession` in harness.ps1,
   which registers a scheduled task with `-LogonType Interactive` so it runs in
   session 1, and writes its output to a file to be read back over SSH.

4. **Resolution.** Without a GCE virtual display device the guest falls back to
   Microsoft Basic Display Adapter with no EDID = 640x480, and the app's own
   window is 760x500. Fix (requires the instance to be STOPPED):

       gcloud compute instances stop   jusprin-win-test --zone=us-central1-a --project=elegoo-backend
       gcloud compute instances update jusprin-win-test --zone=us-central1-a --project=elegoo-backend --enable-display-device
       gcloud compute instances start  jusprin-win-test --zone=us-central1-a --project=elegoo-backend

   Then 1920x1080 is available via set-res.ps1.

## Also required by this app

Microsoft Edge WebView2 runtime is NOT present on a clean Windows Server image.
Without it the app puts up a modal "WebView2 Runtime" prompt and startup blocks
forever. Installed here as 152.0.4191.66 via the Evergreen bootstrapper:

    Invoke-WebRequest "https://go.microsoft.com/fwlink/p/?LinkId=2124703" -OutFile setup.exe
    .\setup.exe /silent /install

This matters more for JusPrin than for stock Orca, since JusPrin's UI is
WebView-based.

## Files

    startup.ps1      GCE windows-startup-script-ps1: OpenSSH, port 22 firewall,
                     authorized_keys, calls autologon.ps1. Runs every boot.
    autologon.ps1    Creates guitest + sets AutoAdminLogon. Idempotent.
    harness.ps1      Invoke-InSession / Take-Screenshot. Source this first.
    screenshot.ps1   Screen capture. Must run in-session.
    probe.ps1        Lists session 1's real windows to C:\guitest\windows.txt.
    focus-app.ps1    Closes leftover task consoles, maximizes the app window.
    click.ps1        Clicks the "x,y" in C:\guitest\click.txt.
    set-res.ps1      Sets 1920x1080. Must run in-session.
    install-app.ps1  Downloads the app, places the Mesa DLLs beside the .exe.
    run-app.cmd      Launches the app with llvmpipe forced, detached.
    winssh.sh        ssh wrapper. winscp.sh: scp wrapper.

## Typical cycle

    ./winscp.sh <local.ps1> guitest@<IP>:C:/guitest/
    ./winssh.sh '. C:\guitest\harness.ps1; Invoke-InSession -TaskName "X" ...'
    ./winssh.sh '. C:\guitest\harness.ps1; Take-Screenshot'
    ./winscp.sh guitest@<IP>:C:/guitest/shot.png ./shot.png

## Known gap

There is no current JusPrin Windows binary to test. The Build all workflow's
Windows job fails at `cmake -G "Visual Studio 17 2022"` with "could not find any
instance of Visual Studio"; last green Windows build was 2026-03-04 and its
artifacts have expired. Either fix that job, or install VS Build Tools on this VM
and build from the cached OrcaSlicer_dep_win64 artifact.

    slicer build 23.0 min
    output       C:\src\JusPrin\build\src\Release\orca-slicer.exe (261 KB launcher)
                 + OrcaSlicer.dll (122.7 MB — the actual application)

## Order of operations

1. `install-buildtools.ps1` — CMake 4.3.5 (CI pins ~4.3.0), Ninja, Git for
   Windows, Strawberry Perl, and VS 2022 Build Tools with the VCTools workload.
2. Clone the repo (public, no credentials needed). Shallow is fine: the version
   comes from `version.inc`, not git tags.
3. `build-deps-full.ps1` — builds all deps. **Do not use the CI dependency
   artifact**; see below.
4. `build-slicer.ps1` — runs `build_release_vs.bat slicer`.
5. Put Mesa where the app looks for it, then `run-jusprin.cmd`.

## Things that will bite you

**Run long builds as a SCHEDULED TASK, not over SSH.** Windows OpenSSH kills the
whole process tree when the session ends, so a build started from an SSH command
(even detached with Start-Process) dies on disconnect. Register it instead:

    New-ScheduledTaskPrincipal -UserId "SYSTEM" -LogonType ServiceAccount -RunLevel Highest

Two builds racing in one directory corrupt each other — OpenSSL failed with
`C1033: cannot open program database ossl_static.pdb` when that happened here.

**awk must be on PATH.** `deps/PNG/PNG.cmake` passes `-DPNG_PREFIX=prusaslicer_`,
so libpng generates `pngprefix.h` with an awk script. Without awk you get
`AWK-NOTFOUND` in the PNG CMakeCache and then `C1083: Cannot open include file:
'pngprefix.h'`. Git for Windows ships awk — add `C:\Program Files\Git\usr\bin`
to PATH, not just `C:\Program Files\Git\cmd`.

**Set `CMAKE_POLICY_VERSION_MINIMUM=3.5`.** Several bundled CMakeLists still
declare pre-3.5 minimums, which CMake 4.x rejects outright.

**The CI dependency artifact is unusable.** `OrcaSlicer_dep_win64_20260906`
contains a bundle built 2025-10-17, before `deps/Eigen` was added. The source
requires Eigen 5.0.1 and CMake fails at configure with "Could not find a package
configuration file provided by Eigen3". Build deps from source instead.

**Never hard-stop the VM mid-build.** Stopping the instance during the deps build
left 622 of 22,011 installed files as NUL bytes. It surfaced as bogus syntax
errors deep in Boost headers. Detect it with:

    Get-ChildItem $prefix -Recurse -Include *.hpp,*.h,*.cmake |
      # read first 4 KB, flag any file containing byte 0

The fix is a clean rebuild; DL_CACHE keeps all 21 source archives, so it is a
recompile, not a re-download.

**Qhull is expected to be missing.** `deps/CMakeLists.txt` comments it out under
`if (MSVC)` ("Experimental"), so 24 built deps is the complete set on Windows.

## Running it — use the app's own Mesa hook

Do NOT drop opengl32.dll next to the exe. `src/OrcaSlicer_app_msvc.cpp` already
handles this: when system OpenGL is below 2.0 it loads `<exedir>\mesa\opengl32.dll`
itself and prints "MESA OpenGL library was loaded successfully".

    build\src\Release\mesa\opengl32.dll      <- Mesa's, the app loads this
    build\src\Release\libgallium_wgl.dll     <- dependency, resolves from exe dir

Still export `GALLIUM_DRIVER=llvmpipe` and `LIBGL_ALWAYS_SOFTWARE=1`: the GCE
virtual display exposes a D3D12 device, and Mesa's d3d12 backend crashes on the
first rendered frame.

## Windows CI is broken for a different reason

`Build all`'s Windows job fails at `cmake -G "Visual Studio 17 2022"` with
"could not find any instance of Visual Studio". That is NOT a bug in
`build_release_vs.bat` — the same script picks generator VS 17 2022 here from
`msbuild -version` (17.14.51.32402) and configures fine against a registered
Build Tools instance. The problem is the GitHub runner's environment.

with its Agent UI visible. Verified 2026-09-07 on n2-standard-16: deps 22.7 min,
slicer 23.0 min. Output is `orca-slicer.exe` (261 KB launcher) plus

**Why:** four of the five failures below produce misleading errors far from
their cause, and two were self-inflicted by how the build was driven.

**How to apply:**
- Run long builds as a Windows **scheduled task** (SYSTEM / ServiceAccount), not
  over SSH — OpenSSH kills the process tree on disconnect. Never let two builds
  share a directory: that produced OpenSSL `C1033 cannot open program database`.
- Add `C:\Program Files\Git\usr\bin` to PATH so **awk** is found, or libpng
  cannot generate `pngprefix.h` (`-DPNG_PREFIX=` in deps/PNG/PNG.cmake) and you
  get a confusing `C1083` on a header that was never written.
- Set `CMAKE_POLICY_VERSION_MINIMUM=3.5` for CMake 4.x.
- **Do not use the CI deps artifact** — the shipped bundle predates `deps/Eigen`
  and cannot satisfy Eigen 5.0.1. Build deps from source.
- Never hard-stop the VM mid-build: doing so left 622 installed files full of
  NUL bytes and surfaced as fake syntax errors inside Boost headers.
- Qhull is deliberately excluded on MSVC (deps/CMakeLists.txt), so 24/25 is
  complete on Windows.
- To run headless, use the app's own hook rather than dropping DLLs beside the
  exe: `src/OrcaSlicer_app_msvc.cpp` loads `<exedir>\mesa\opengl32.dll` when
  system OpenGL < 2.0. Still force `GALLIUM_DRIVER=llvmpipe`.

The `Build all` Windows CI job fails at `cmake -G "Visual Studio 17 2022"` with
"could not find any instance of Visual Studio". That is a GitHub runner
environment problem, not `build_release_vs.bat` — the same script selects the
same generator on the VM and configures fine against registered Build Tools.

**MSVC rejects `this` in a nested lambda's init-capture.** Found 2026-09-07 at
commit fbe5963b: `CallAfter([self=wxWeakRef<wxWindow>(this),...])` written INSIDE
another lambda compiled on clang but failed on MSVC with 37 errors, because MSVC
bound that `this` to the enclosing closure object, so it tried to build a
`wxWeakRef<wxWindow>` from a lambda pointer
(`Tracked_class_should_inherit_from_wxTrackable`). Name the object first —
`auto* menu = this;` then capture `menu`. Watch for this pattern whenever a
deferred callback is set up from within another lambda; it is invisible on macOS.

**PowerShell splits `-m:6` (2026-10-24).** In a .ps1, `& cmake --build … -- -m:6 -v:m`
reaches MSBuild as `-m:` `6` and fails at once ("For switch syntax, type
MSBuild -help"). Quote them: `'-m:6' '-v:m'`. Also `*>>` writes UTF-16, so
Select-String on that log matches nothing; use `2>&1 | Out-File -Encoding utf8`.
A watcher built from `winssh.sh 'powershell -Command "…\"…\"…"'` silently never
matched for 3 hours — the quoting rule above applies to status checks too.
Killing "my" processes by command-line match also took out a taskhostw.exe;
kill the PIDs your own task started (and their /T trees), not a pattern.

**Shell harness on the VM (2026-11-07, app-menus).** `C:\src\JusPrin\build\tests\shell\Release\shell_integration_harness.exe` has Mesa beside it; run it from a .cmd with `GALLIUM_DRIVER=llvmpipe` and `LIBGL_ALWAYS_SOFTWARE=1` through an Interactive scheduled task as guitest; it uses its own temp data dir. Build it with `cmake --build build --config Release --target jusprin_web shell_integration_harness -- '-m:12'` (node is at `C:\Users\guitest\.local\node-v24.21.0-win-x64`). The VM has no access to unpushed commits: send them with `git bundle create f.bundle <branch> ^<vm-head>`.
- MSVC also rejects a local `constexpr` used inside a lambda that doesn't capture it (C3493; clang accepts). Make it `static constexpr`.
- On jusprin-newui b0a2fe3b08 the default suite already fails 6 checks on Windows: three failed_autosave_* checks (the harness simulates a failed save by removing write permission, and Windows ignores that on folders), earlier_model_version_available, and agent_panel_columns_tile_the_client at 1000 and 1400 DIP. Compare against that list before blaming a change.
- In PowerShell, `[IO.File]` takes relative paths from the process folder, not from Set-Location; use absolute paths. In a .cmd, `echo exit=%ERRORLEVEL%>> f` turns `0>>` into a redirect; put a space before `>>`.

  startup on a certificate-store dialog.

  for /run/xrdp/xrdp.pid, the folder is gone, and the tunnel prints "channel 2:
  open failed: connect failed: Connection refused". Fix:
  `sudo systemctl restart xrdp-sesman xrdp`, then `ss -ltn | grep 3389`.
- `pkill -f orca-slicer` over ssh kills the ssh session itself; use `pkill -x`.
- Homebrew moved openssl@3 to @4 on 2026-11-09 and broke gcloud's Python;
  env.sh sets CLOUDSDK_PYTHON to uv's standalone CPython 3.12.

# JusPrin Linux GUI test VM

A GCP VM for building JusPrin on Linux and testing its GUI, either by hand over
remote desktop or by script on a headless display.

| | |
|---|---|
| Instance | `jusprin-linux-test`, project `elegoo-backend`, zone `us-west2-a` (Los Angeles, for low latency from California) |
| Machine | n2-standard-16 (16 vCPU, 64 GB), 300 GB pd-balanced, no GPU |
| OS | Ubuntu 24.04 LTS, XFCE desktop |
| Toolchain | Ubuntu's gcc 13, CMake 4.3.0 (same as the CI runner, in /opt), Node 24.11.1 (in /opt) |
| Checkout | `~/JusPrin` on branch `jusprin-dev` (user `kenneth`) |
| OpenGL | Mesa llvmpipe, OpenGL 4.5 core, software rendering |

The VM has no service account, so it cannot call GCP APIs. It cannot fetch the
private GitHub repo either; send commits with a git bundle (below).

## Scripts (run on the Mac)

- `./vmssh.sh '<command>'` runs a command on the VM.
- `./vmscp.sh <src> <dst>` copies files; write `VM:~/path` for the VM side.
- `./connect-rdp.sh` starts the VM if stopped, prints the login, and holds an SSH
  tunnel open. Point Windows App (Microsoft Remote Desktop) at `localhost:33890`,
  user `kenneth`. xrdp listens only on the VM's own localhost, so the project-wide
  `default-allow-rdp` firewall rule does not expose it.
- `env.sh` holds the instance name and forces the `ai-agent` service account. It
  also points gcloud at uv's standalone Python 3.12, because Homebrew's Python lost
  its OpenSSL library when Homebrew moved from openssl@3 to openssl@4.

## Scripts (copied to the VM's home folder)

- `~/vm-run-app.sh [args]` starts the built app on headless display `:99` (Xvfb
  with the xfwm4 window manager) with data dir `~/jusprin-test-data`. Log:
  `~/app.log`. It sets `SSL_CERT_FILE`; without it OrcaSlicer's Linux build stops
  at startup on a dialog asking which certificate file to use.
- `~/vm-screenshot.sh` saves display `:99` to `~/shot.png`.
- Click with `DISPLAY=:99 xdotool mousemove X Y click 1`. Screenshot pixels equal
  screen coordinates (1920x1080).
- Stop the app with `pkill -x orca-slicer`. Never `pkill -f orca-slicer` over
  ssh: it matches the ssh command's own text and kills the session.

## Build

```bash
# First time on a fresh VM: deps (about 25 min) then app and tests (about 30 min)
cd ~/JusPrin && ./build_linux.sh -dst -j 16
# After code changes: app and tests only
cd ~/JusPrin && ./build_linux.sh -st -j 16
```

The app lands in `~/JusPrin/build/package/bin/orca-slicer`. Run long builds
detached so an ssh disconnect does not kill them:

```bash
setsid nohup bash -c 'set -o pipefail; ./build_linux.sh -st -j 16 2>&1 | tee ~/build.log; echo BUILD_EXIT=$? >> ~/build.log' >/dev/null 2>&1 </dev/null &
```

Tests: `cd ~/JusPrin/build && DISPLAY=:99 ctest -C Release -j 8`.

## Sending new commits

```bash
git bundle create f.bundle jusprin-dev ^<commit the VM already has>
./vmscp.sh f.bundle VM:~/
./vmssh.sh 'cd ~/JusPrin && git pull ~/f.bundle jusprin-dev'
```

## Cost

The VM bills while running. Stop it when idle:

```bash
gcloud compute instances stop jusprin-linux-test --project elegoo-backend --zone us-west2-a
```

The external IP is ephemeral and changes on each start; the scripts look it up
by name, so nothing needs editing.

VM=jusprin-linux-test
PROJECT=elegoo-backend
ZONE=us-west2-a
gcloud config set account ai-agent@tsdtechnology.iam.gserviceaccount.com >/dev/null 2>&1
# Homebrew's Python lost its OpenSSL (openssl@3 -> @4) on 2026-11-09; use uv's
# self-contained CPython for gcloud when it is present.
UVPY=/Users/kenneth/.local/share/uv/python/cpython-3.12.9-macos-aarch64-none/bin/python3.12
[ -x "$UVPY" ] && export CLOUDSDK_PYTHON="$UVPY"

input.content:
# JusPrin 2.0.1: error-handling audit findings

Range audited: tag `jusprin/v2.0.0` to `262fe08e91` (origin/jusprin-dev on
2026-11-17), and the tsd-enterprise commits under `web_ent/jusprin/` on
`master` since 2026-11-12. Four agents read the code against the Error
handling section of AGENTS.md and the `error-handling` skill. Every finding
was checked by reading only; nothing was run to confirm it. Under the bug-fix
rule, any finding chosen for fixing is reproduced first.

## Bugs a person would hit (new in this range)

1. **The report dialog promises less than the report holds.**
   `Shell/ErrorReportDialog.cpp:116-117, 141-143, 225-234` and the
   Preferences line (`AgentUI/src/components/Preferences.tsx:657`) say the
   report is only the lines shown, with "no files, no project names", and
   that "JusPrin's server sees your IP address". Since a14e9d762f every
   report also carries this run's log file (`Support/SentryClient.cpp:159-166`),
   the native stack, the loaded modules and the machine; the home folder is no
   longer trimmed; and it goes to Sentry, not JusPrin's server. For the app's
   own reports the dialog says "That is the whole report" while a stack and
   the log go with it. Kenneth's "Keep the promise and accept the risk" was
   about error text, before the log was attached.
2. **An AI reply can spin forever.** If starting the request
   (`AgentHost.cpp:3034`, `ProviderAgent.cpp:462`) or continuing after a tool
   result (`AgentHost.cpp:3410`, `ProviderAgent.cpp:585`) throws, the reply is
   never ended as failed. The chat stays busy until the person presses Stop.
   With automatic reports on, nothing tells them anything.
3. **A printer card on Home can freeze for the rest of the run.**
   `Printers/HostLaneReader.cpp:213-216`: if one status read throws, the
   reader's bookkeeping is skipped, so that printer is never read again until
   restart, and quitting waits 3 seconds.
4. **The printer chat can stay on "Checking <address>".** A connection test
   that throws (now any of about a dozen OrcaSlicer host tests,
   `PrinterSetup/OrcaPrinterBackend.cpp:206-211, 857-876`) never ends the
   `printer_host_connect` call, and the error goes to OrcaSlicer's main-loop
   handler instead of JusPrin's report.
5. **Dropping a file on Home can fail on Windows for non-ASCII names.**
   `Support/Files.cpp:16` builds the temp path with `path.string() + ".tmp"`,
   which on Windows converts through the ANSI code page. A file or data
   folder name outside it throws, and the error dialog opens.
6. **A page error during the page's first moments reaches nobody.**
   `WebShared/bridgeClient.ts:104` installs the error handlers only after the
   first render. An error before that leaves a blank AI panel or blank Home,
   with no dialog and no report. Reports queued before the handshake are also
   dropped if it never completes (`bridgeClient.ts:155`).
7. **A failed print report can end in silence.**
   `HomeUI/src/components/PrintReportForm.tsx:51-55,138` re-enables Send with
   no sentence, relying on the app's dialog, which does not open when
   automatic reports are on or the same failure was answered earlier.

## Rule findings: sentences, codes or branches nobody decided

App:
- Every connection failure, including a 120-second timeout, a TLS failure and
  a reply cut off partway, reads "The AI request could not reach the %1%
  service." and is not reported (`ProviderAgent.cpp:702`).
- Rate limiting keeps "Try again shortly" (`ProviderAgent.cpp:675, 738, 753`),
  which the rules call unexpected.
- Sign-in: any 4xx from our own server, including 429 and 403, reads
  "JusPrin couldn't sign you in. Try again." and is not reported
  (`CloudAccount.cpp:308`).
- Model list: 4xx answers from our own gateway are only logged
  (`ModelCatalog.cpp:196`, `AgentConfiguration.cpp:382`).
- Delete account: any non-204, and also a printer or filament chat still
  replying, reads "Check your internet connection, then try again."
  (`ModelCatalogFetch.cpp:155`, `Preferences.tsx:281,296`). A commit says
  this wording is still to be decided.
- Every failed file open or import is "refused" and never reported
  (`Workspace/OrcaWorkspaceAdapter.cpp:2631, 2807`).
- MCP setup refusals are new designed outcomes with no quoted yes; one shows
  nlohmann's raw parse error (`Mcp/McpConfigFile.cpp:186`).
- A model's third invalid tool call now opens the error dialog
  (`ProviderAgent.cpp:568, 585`); the rules say it goes to the model.
- The generic error offers Retry (`AgentHost.cpp:615`).
- Account pages: a server fault on the web link reads "Check your internet
  connection" and is not reported (`Shell/ServerSheet.cpp:85-95, 214`).
- Unreadable printer profiles show "The printer profiles could not be read:
  %1%" instead of a report (`PrinterSetup/SetupOptionsLoader.cpp:83-86`).
- A failure already answered once is never asked about again this run
  (`Support/ErrorReport.cpp:112-114`); b3eed3bf4b recorded the opposite, and
  3c134d39e3 changed it without a quote.
- Smaller: `ErrorReport.cpp:164-166` loses the error text when no path is
  found in it; `Home/HomeWebView.cpp:168` can throw inside its own catch;
  `Updates/LaunchReport.cpp:42` has no `reported()` around its callback;
  `AgentUI/src/i18n.tsx:33` silently falls back when a catalog is missing.

Server (tsd-enterprise `master`):
- `invalid_request`, `unknown_model` and `method_not_allowed` keep sentences
  of their own, although the code comment quotes Kenneth: "Treat them as
  unexpected errors" (`errors.py:68-75`, `gateway.py:161-166, 194-196`).
- "Chat too large" is detected only by the provider answering 413

input.ask: Deploy the server, and fix the seven user-facing audit bugs before release?

content.text:
Release 2.0.1 is ready up to the point where I need your answers. Nothing is committed or pushed yet.

**Done so far.** The main checkout was clean and fully pushed. The release covers 20 commits, from tag `jusprin/v2.0.0` to `262fe08e91`, in a new worktree at `/Users/kenneth/Projects/JusPrin/.claude/worktrees/release-2.0.1` on branch `claude/release-2.0.1`. In it I set `kVersion` to 2.0.1 and drafted the release notes. The error-handling audit is finished. Test builds are running on this Mac and on both VMs, and the Linux build has already compiled.

**Decision needed: deploying the server.** Production `jusprinv2.obico.io` is missing all five JusPrin server commits made on tsd-enterprise `master` since 2.0.0, and 2.0.1 depends on them.
- `/ent/jusprin/v2/launches` answers 404. 2.0.1 sends its start report there every time it starts. Anyone with automatic error reports on would send a Sentry report on every start.
- Server text stays English: I sent a German request and got English back.

Every other address the app calls answered. Deploying is your call, and so is whether you do it or I do. My pick is to deploy before the release workflow runs. Should the server be deployed now?

**Decision needed: which audit findings to fix before release.** The full list is in `/Users/kenneth/Library/Application Support/Claude/side-session-notes/local_55a7089d-34d6-4d0c-bc2e-c3745b488d0d/release-2.0.1-audit-findings.md`. I found these by reading the code; none is confirmed by running it yet. I'd fix these seven, because a person would run into each one:
1. **The report's privacy promise is wrong.** The report dialog and Preferences say a report has "no files, no project names" and that JusPrin's server sees the IP address. Since the Sentry commit, every report also carries the run's log file (with home-folder paths no longer trimmed) and the native stack, and it goes to Sentry. This one needs new wording from you, translated into 22 languages, or a change to what is sent.
2. **An AI reply can spin forever.** If the request fails while starting, or after a tool result, the reply is never ended, so it spins until the person presses Stop.
3. **A printer card on Home can freeze.** After one failed status read, that printer is never read again until restart.
4. **The printer chat can get stuck.** If a connection test throws, the chat stays on "Checking <address>" for any of the newly allowed host types.
5. **Dropping a file on Home can fail on Windows.** A file or folder name outside the ANSI code page makes it fail.
6. **An early page error is lost.** An error in a page's first moments leaves a blank panel, and nothing reports it.
7. **A failed print report can say nothing.** When automatic reports are on, the person gets no word that it failed.

There are also about 20 rule findings: sentences or codes for failures nobody decided, in the app and on the server. Examples are "could not reach" shown for timeouts and "Check your internet connection" shown for a server fault. My pick is to leave those for after 2.0.1. Each fix gets reproduced first, is its own commit on `jusprin-dev`, and restarts the checks for the grown range. Which of these should be fixed before release?

**Decision needed: the release notes wording.** They are in [2.0.1.md](.claude/worktrees/release-2.0.1/src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/Packaging/release-notes/2.0.1.md). They cover:
- **New:** the 22 languages, every print host type in the printer chat (Elegoo Centauri included), and the "Something went wrong on our side" report.
- **Fixed:** eight bugs, including issue #39's missing nozzle sizes in comma-decimal languages.
- **What JusPrin now sends:** a section on the start report and the error reports.

I checked every on-screen label against the source. Is that wording right, or what should change?

**Decision needed: a paid AI check.** The prompt tests also come in a small paid run on the app's default model, `gpt-5.4-mini`, which the testing notes ask for before a release. The last comparable full batch cost about $0.50, and I'd expect $1–3. I'll run the free version on your Claude subscription either way. Should I spend that money on the paid run?

One more thing: Sentry now has to be in the dependency build. Kenneth's main checkout's dependency build didn't have it, so I built Sentry on its own in my scratchpad and didn't touch the shared build.

# Handoff: seven error-handling bugs to fix for the release after 2.0.1

Kenneth, 2026-11-17, during the 2.0.1 release: "create a handoff doc for the 7
bugs for the next release". 2.0.1 ships without these fixes.

The error-handling audit of the 2.0.1 range (tag `jusprin/v2.0.0` to
`262fe08e91`) found them. Each was found **by reading the code only**. None
has been reproduced yet. AGENTS.md's bug-fix rule applies: reproduce each one
in the local dev environment first, show it failing, then fix it and show it
passing. If one cannot be reproduced, stop and tell Kenneth instead of fixing
it. Each fix is its own commit on a branch from `origin/jusprin-dev`, and the
error-handling rules in AGENTS.md ("Error handling") decide what the fixed code
may do.

The line numbers are from `262fe08e91`. They may have moved since.

The audit also found about 20 smaller rule findings, in the app and in the
server: sentences or codes for failures nobody decided. They are listed in
`/Users/kenneth/Library/Application Support/Claude/side-session-notes/local_55a7089d-34d6-4d0c-bc2e-c3745b488d0d/release-2.0.1-audit-findings.md`
under "Rule findings". They are not part of this handoff.

## 1. The error report promises less than it sends

**What the person sees.** The "Something went wrong on our side" dialog says
the report is only the lines shown: "That is the whole report. It has no chat
messages, no files, no project names and no account or email address."
Preferences › Updates › Error reports says the same and adds "JusPrin's server
sees your IP address, as with any web page."

**What is actually sent.** Since a14e9d762f (reports go straight to Sentry)
every report also carries this run's log file
(`Support/SentryClient.cpp:159-166`), the native stack, the loaded modules
and the machine. The home folder is no longer replaced by "~", and the report
goes to Sentry, not JusPrin's server. For the app's own reports the dialog's
"Where" row is empty, so it says "That is the whole report" while a stack and
the log go with it. The log can name project files and folders.

**Where.** `Shell/ErrorReportDialog.cpp:116-117, 141-143, 225-234`,
`AgentUI/src/components/Preferences.tsx:657`.

**Needs Kenneth.** This is a wording decision or a decision about what to
send, not a code fix alone. His earlier "Keep the promise and accept the
risk" (b3eed3bf4b) was about error text, before the log was attached. Bring
him the choice: make the sentences say what is sent (new wording, translated
into the 22 languages), or send less (no log file, home folder trimmed again,
which he had removed: "delete both older trims"). Do not pick for him.
Before writing any sentence that says what a report never holds, check what
the log file can contain.

## 2. An AI reply can spin forever

**What the person sees.** The reply spinner never stops, and the chat stays
busy until they press Stop. With automatic reports on, no dialog opens, so
nothing tells them anything.

**Cause found by reading.** Only `pump_stream`'s handler
(`Agent/AgentHost.cpp:3442`) ends a reply as failed. Two other paths can
throw without ending it:
- starting the request: `begin_stream` calls `m_agent->start` at
  `AgentHost.cpp:3034`, which can throw from `post()`
  (`ProviderAgent.cpp:462`) or from `keep_blob`'s write;
- continuing after a tool result: `continue_after_tool`
  (`AgentHost.cpp:3410`) can throw from `next_call` (`ProviderAgent.cpp:585`)
  or its `post()`.

The throw reaches the page-message handler or the shell timer's
`reported(...)`, is reported under the wrong "was doing", and `fail_stream`
never runs, so `m_stream` stays set.

## 3. A printer card on Home can freeze for the rest of the run

**What the person sees.** One printer's card on Home stops updating and shows
its last reading until the app restarts. Quitting waits 3 seconds.

**Cause found by reading.** `Printers/HostLaneReader.cpp:213-216` wraps the
read thread in `reported()`. If `read()` throws, `shared->finish(...)` and
`--running` are skipped. The printer stays marked in flight, so `begin()`
never reads it again this run. The failure is reported once.

## 4. The printer chat can stay on "Checking <address>"

**What the person sees.** After asking AI to connect a printer, the chat
stays on "Checking <address>" and never answers.

**Cause found by reading.** f88b40865c lets `printer_host_connect` run
OrcaSlicer's own connection test for about a dozen host types
(`PrinterSetup/OrcaPrinterBackend.cpp:206-211`). If that test throws, the end
callback (lines 871-876) returns without calling `tested`, so the tool call
never ends. `BoostThreadWorker::process_events`
(`Jobs/BoostThreadWorker.cpp:35-36`) then rethrows inside JusPrin's idle
handler (lines 857-860), which has no `reported()`. So the error goes to
OrcaSlicer's main-loop handler instead of JusPrin's report.

## 5. Dropping a file on Home can fail on Windows

**What the person sees.** Dropping a file on Home opens the error dialog when
the file's name or the data folder's path has characters outside the Windows
code page. Example: Chinese characters on an English Windows.

**Cause found by reading.** `Support/Files.cpp:16`, new in this range, builds
the temporary path as `path.string() + ".tmp"`. On Windows, `string()`
converts through the ANSI code page and throws for characters it cannot hold.
Reproduce on the Windows test VM.

## 6. An early page error reaches nobody

**What the person sees.** A blank AI panel or a blank Home, with no dialog.
Sentry gets nothing.

**Cause found by reading.** `WebShared/bridgeClient.ts:104` installs the
page's error handlers inside `client.start()`, which runs from a `useEffect`
after the first render (`AgentUI/src/App.tsx:149-150`,
`HomeUI/src/App.tsx:67-68` and the other `*App.tsx` files). Before that, the
language is activated on import (`i18n.tsx:62`) and modules build translated
text at their top level (`credits.ts` `TIER_NAMES`, `SIGNUP_OFFER`;
`history.ts` `REPORT_OFFER`). An error there or in the first render has no
handler.

Also: reports queued before the handshake (`bridgeClient.ts:155`) are sent
only on `hello_ack` (line 180). They are lost if the handshake ends in
timeout, no transport or incompatible, which is when one may explain why the
page failed to connect.

## 7. A failed print report can end in silence

**What the person sees.** On Home's Print history they press Send on a print
report. They see "Sending…", then the button comes back and nothing is said.

**Cause found by reading.** `HomeUI/src/components/PrintReportForm.tsx:51-55,138`:
the `'unexpected'` state only re-enables Send, relying on the app's dialog.
But `Support/ErrorReport.cpp:108-114` opens no dialog when automatic reports
are on, or when the same failure was already answered earlier in the run.
The API-key form handles the same case by showing "Something went wrong on our
side" itself (`AgentUI/src/components/AgentConnection.tsx:411`).

13:## Before a release
14-
15-The guide is brought in line with the app before each release, on a computer with the app built.
16-
17-1. Build the app's test harness and pages from the commit to release: the `shell_integration_harness` and `jusprin_web` targets.
18-2. Leave the computer alone and run `scripts/check_guide.py --ask-ai`. It takes about a minute a page, plus the questions.
19-3. Fix what it reports, then run it again until it passes:
20-   - **A label is on no screen.** The app's wording changed. Find the new wording in the app and correct the page.
21-   - **A run failed.** Open its log, which the command names. Either the screen no longer works as the page says, and the page needs correcting, or the harness expects something the app no longer does, and the harness needs correcting.
22-   - **A picture is blank.** The program that started the command may not record the screen. Grant it Screen Recording in the system's privacy settings and run again.
23-   - **AI answered a question wrongly.** Read its reply in the output. Usually the page is unclear or its first line does not say when to read it.
24-4. Look through what changed on screen since the last release (`git log <last release tag>..HEAD -- src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin`). The command finds what a page gets wrong. It cannot find a new screen or menu item that no page mentions, so add those by hand.
25-5. Commit the pages together with their pictures, the skills the command rebuilt, and `checked-version.txt`. When every step passes for every page, the command writes the app's version to that file. A run with `--skip-app`, with `--area`, or without `--ask-ai` leaves it as it was. The release workflow refuses a version this file does not name. The file says the check passed for that version, not on which commit, so run it on the commit you mean to release.

30-2. **Rebuilds the copy AI reads.** `src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/AgentUI/src/guide.ts` builds a skill from each page.

## Classic view

Classic view is the app's original screen, with all print settings in a panel at the side. Choose **Switch to classic view…** in the **View** menu, or in the "…" menu at the right of the header. JusPrin looks for a newer version once a day, on GitHub. When there is one, **Updates** in Preferences is marked with a dot.

1. In Preferences, open **Updates**. **Check now** looks straight away.

## Running on the Claude subscription (`--backend claude-cli`)

`--backend claude-cli` answers every step with the locally installed Claude
Code CLI in headless mode (`claude -p`), billed to the developer's Claude
subscription instead of a per-token API key. `--judge claude-cli` moves the
judge there as well. Neither needs a key; both need the CLI logged in once
with `claude auth login`. The runner refuses to start a run the CLI would bill
to an API key (`apiKeySource` other than the login).

tests/project_prompt/run_prompt_tests.py --backend claude-cli --judge claude-cli --case advice-infill --runs 1

`--claude-judge-model`). `--claude-keep DIR` keeps each run's session file,
tool list, MCP config and the CLI's event stream for reading afterwards.

content.text:
I compared this release with 2.0.0 on the three prompt cases that failed some runs. Their results come out about the same:

| Case | This release | 2.0.0 |
|---|---|---|
| Printer chat: Klipper shut down | 10 of 12 passed | 11 of 12 passed |
| Printer chat: no API key | 9 of 12 passed | 8 of 12 passed |
| Project chat: "I want to print this" | 1 failed out of 6 | 1 failed out of 6 |

So 2.0.1 did not cause these failures; they were already there in 2.0.0. In both versions the printer-chat failures are the same two wording misses: not saying the printer can't print until Klipper restarts, and stating a Mainsail menu path as fact.

In the project-chat case, more runs this time came back with no result to judge (3 of 6, against 1 of 6). That happens when the AI goes on after starting a slice, past the end of the saved test recording. It isn't a failure. My guess, not verified, is that this release's change telling the AI not to keep checking a slice it started means more replies continue past that point. Either way, these are older problems for you to decide on, not blockers for 2.0.1.

The guide check and the Windows tests are still running. Please keep leaving the Mac alone while the guide check uses the screen.

content.text:
The Windows tests finished with 3,916 of 3,920 passing. I've fixed three of the four failures, and the fourth looks older than this release.

**The three I fixed.** Commit 3c134d39e3 in this release added three tests that fail only on Windows. The app code they check is fine; the tests themselves are wrong on Windows:
- **Folder permissions:** two tests make a file unreadable, or a folder impossible to remove, by changing its permissions. Windows ignores those permissions, so the failure the test expects never happens. Those checks now run only on Mac and Linux, which is how `test_mcp_discovery.cpp` already handles the same limitation.
- **Text mode:** one test wrote its sample G-code in text mode, so on Windows the file came out 7 bytes instead of 6. It now writes in binary mode, the same fix as commit 70f08918d8. Its permission-based check also now runs only on Mac and Linux.

With the fix applied on the Windows VM, `agent_bridge_tests` passes all 606 test cases. The fix is commit `ec016dc5e3`, on branch `claude/windows-permission-tests` in its own worktree at `/Users/kenneth/Projects/JusPrin/.claude/worktrees/windows-permission-tests`. It changes 3 test files, 11 lines added and 1 removed, and it isn't pushed.

**The fourth failure: "a menu row's second line takes the role it is given".** That test existed in 2.0.0. This release didn't change the test, the menu row it measures, or the design tokens it reads, so I believe it fails on 2.0.0 too. I couldn't prove that by building 2.0.0: the Windows VM's disk is nearly full, with 3.4 GB free of 536 GB, mostly other sessions' worktrees, which I left alone.

**After the push.** I'd rebase the release branch onto it and re-run the checks the release skill requires for the new range: the tests on all three platforms and the guide check. The release notes, translations and server need nothing new, since the fix only touches tests.

The first guide check is still using this Mac's screen, so please keep leaving it alone.

Summary:
1. Primary Request and Intent:
   - This session was started by another Claude session (local_55a7089d-34d6-4d0c-bc2e-c3745b488d0d) with the task: "Make JusPrin release 2.0.1 by following the `jusprin-release` skill." Kenneth, the project owner, wants version 2.0.1, and I must ask him in this session whenever the skill says to. The shared notes folder is `/Users/kenneth/Library/Application Support/Claude/side-session-notes/local_55a7089d-34d6-4d0c-bc2e-c3745b488d0d`.
