     - the version (given: 2.0.1)
     - the release notes' wording (done: "Notes are fine")
     - deploying the server (done: "deploy the server")
     - which error-handling findings to fix (he chose to defer the seven bugs to a handoff doc)
     - taking in commits that landed after the range was fixed
     - the Sentry values and a read-only token for checking the draft
     - spending API money (paid prompt run: asked twice, never answered, so not approved)
     - pushing to jusprin-dev and moving main
     - starting the release workflow
     - downloading the draft's files
     - posting on GitHub
   - **Never publish the draft** (Kenneth publishes it by hand). **Never force-push main.**
   - Kenneth's explicit messages: "deploy the server. create a handoff doc for the 7 bugs for the next release"; "Notes are fine"; "Yes, push it" (for the Windows test fix ec016dc5e3).

2. Key Technical Concepts:
   - JusPrin is a fork of OrcaSlicer: C++17, wxWidgets, CMake/Ninja, Catch2 tests, and the AgentUI/HomeUI pages (React, Lingui, vitest).
   - The release workflow `.github/workflows/jusprin_release.yml` needs:
     - the version above every released one
     - the release notes file
     - `docs/guide/checked-version.txt` matching the version
     - five Sentry secrets
   - The skill's fix rule. Any fix is its own commit on jusprin-dev, made in its own worktree. Before section 8 lands the release commit: commit the release edits, rebase onto origin/jusprin-dev, record the new range end, then redo step 1.4 and sections 2–7.
   - Error-handling rules are in the AGENTS.md "Error handling" section. Only expected errors (the person can act on them, and Kenneth decided the wording) get their own sentences. Everything else is reported through `report_unexpected_error` and the person sees "Something went wrong on our side".
   - Server deploy flow:
     - tsd-enterprise `release.sh` builds the `release` branch, and CircleCI builds image `kennethjiang/web_ent:obi.NNNN`.
     - In the ops repo `~/Projects/ops/tsd/`, `stg/update-version.sh OLD NEW` swaps the tag in both stg and prod yamls. Then `stg/release-stg.sh` applies staging, and `prod/release.sh` applies prod 60 s apart.
     - The prod script also waits 1200 s, then scales tsdws-prod 12→11→10, 300 s per step.
     - The migration runs in the tsdweb initContainer.
   - Building on a shared Mac: check load first, use `-j4`, start builds in their own process group, one build per build directory.
   - Windows VM rules:
     - Run builds as SYSTEM scheduled tasks; Windows SSH kills builds when the session ends.
     - The SSH shell is PowerShell.
     - The VM can fetch from GitHub.
     - The disk is nearly full, about 3.4 GB free of 536 GB.
   - The Linux VM cannot reach GitHub; send commits as a git bundle.
   - Prompt suites: `--backend claude-cli --judge claude-cli` runs on the Claude subscription at no API cost. `--prompt-rev REV` compares against an older prompt.
   - zsh does not word-split `$VAR`, so write options out inline.

   - Release worktree `/Users/kenneth/Projects/JusPrin/.claude/worktrees/release-2.0.1`, branch `claude/release-2.0.1`, still at 262fe08e91 with uncommitted edits.
   - `src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/Updates/Version.hpp`: changed to `inline constexpr char kVersion[] = "2.0.1";`.
   - `src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/Packaging/release-notes/2.0.1.md`: new, untracked, approved by Kenneth. Its content, in summary:
     - Opening line: "JusPrin 2.0.1 speaks your language, connects more printers from the printer chat, and fixes printers that could not be added in languages that write decimals with a comma."
     - **## New**
       - JusPrin in your language: 22 languages, set in Preferences › Appearance › Language; numbers follow it ("0,4 mm"); machine-made translations.
       - More printers connect from the printer chat: every connection type, including Elegoo Centauri Carbon and Carbon 2 (Elegoo Link). The chat cannot finish Repetier, UltiMaker, or PrusaLink with a user name and password. Obico, SimplyPrint and 3DPrinterOS need their own sign-in.
       - Reporting errors: the "Something went wrong on our side" dialog, Report to JusPrin team, the "From now on, report errors like this automatically" box, and Preferences › Updates › Error reports, which is off until turned on.
     - **## Fixed** (8 items):
       - comma-decimal nozzle sizes, bed sizes and 3MF nozzle read wrongly
       - a calibration test from a project lost its project and chat
       - a project saved itself again after sitting idle
       - a refused attachment blocked saving
       - a sign-in or API key the settings file couldn't keep now shows an error
       - Delete account waits until AI has finished replying in any chat
       - a chat whose account or key was removed showed the wrong model in its greyed picker
       - AI kept checking a slice it had just started
     - **## What JusPrin now sends**
       - Start report: a random number, the version and the OS name; skipped in stealth mode.
       - Error reports and crashes: go to Sentry only when sent by hand or with automatic reports on. They hold where in the app the error happened, the steps before it (never what was typed or what AI said), the OS, and the run's log; a crash report also holds the app's state; with automatic reports off a crash stays on the computer.

Tick **From now on, report errors like this automatically** to send later ones without asking. content.text:
The 2.0.1 release commit is ready, and every check has been run again on it. It is commit 2236eda028 on branch `claude/release-2.0.1`. It sits directly on top of ec016dc5e3, the Windows test fix you approved earlier, and nobody has pushed to `jusprin-dev` since. Nothing is pushed yet.

**Test results on the release commit:**
- **Linux:** all 3925 tests passed.
- **Mac:** 3915 of 3916 tests passed, plus all 834 AI panel page tests and all 168 Home page tests. The one failure is a test that gives a printer plugin at most 3 seconds to disconnect when the app closes; it waited 137 seconds instead. It ran while other work on this Mac had the load average at about 47. Run alone afterwards, it passed 5 times out of 5, about 3 seconds each. The test comes from OrcaSlicer, is older than 2.0.0, and nothing in this release touches it.
- **Windows:** 3918 of 3919 tests passed. The three tests the Windows fix covered now pass. The one failure is the same as on the first run: a menu row's second line measures 195 pixels where the test expects less. That test is older than 2.0.0 and the code it measures did not change in this release. It is probably an older Windows problem, but I haven't proven that.

**Translations and the guide:**
- Running the catalog update again changed nothing.
- I did not run the guide check again. The only commit added since it passed changes three test files and nothing in the app, and `docs/guide/checked-version.txt` already says 2.0.1.

**Decision needed:** whether to land the release. Pushing changes the shared branches, so it needs your yes.
- **Push both.** The commit goes to `jusprin-dev`, the main checkout is brought along with a fast-forward pull, and `main` is moved to the same commit. `main` is at ff318b33bc, which this commit already contains, so the move is a plain fast-forward with no force. After that, the next step is starting the release workflow, which needs its own yes.
- **Push only `jusprin-dev`.** The release stays on hold, and nothing is built.

My pick is to push both.

# Project chat prompt tests

The project chat's assistant is a system prompt
(`src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/AgentUI/src/projectInstructions.ts`), the project
tools and the chat. `run_prompt_tests.py` asks the live model for its next
step at a known point of a project chat and checks that step against one
sentence of the prompt. After an edit it runs once, on the checkout, and
prints each case beside a baseline kept in the repository (`baseline.json`;
see "Judging a prompt or skill change"). The app does not run.

On Kenneth's local machine, the keys are in
`~/.config/jusprin/prompt-test.env` (outside the repository, mode `600`). An
agent running this suite can load them for that command in a subshell:

```bash
( . "$HOME/.config/jusprin/prompt-test.env"; tests/project_prompt/run_prompt_tests.py )
```

Do not print, copy into the repository, or include the key values in a command
or test log. The file exports `OPENROUTER_API_KEY` and `OPENAI_API_KEY`; the
runner reads them from its environment. No run happens without Kenneth
approving that batch (case count, runs, token estimate). A `403 Key limit
exceeded` means stop; do not switch keys.

The model, hosts and judge are the printer suite's (`tests/printer_prompt`,
"Which model"): DeepSeek V4 Flash through OpenRouter, pinned to Alibaba,
Novita, Baidu and AtlasCloud, with a pinned OpenAI judge. `--backend
claude-cli` runs the same cases on the developer's Claude subscription
instead, for iterating on a prompt without API cost (see "Running on the
Claude subscription").

## Running it

The runner and `test_steps.py` need the app's argument check built:
`cmake --build <build dir> --config <config> --target tool_call_check`. The
runner takes the newest one under `build/` (or `JUSPRIN_TOOL_CALL_CHECK`) and
stops when it is older than `ToolRegistry.cpp`.

By default every case runs 3 times (`RUN_BUDGET` 81 shared by the cases run,
at most 20 for one case alone); `--runs N` sets it. `--verbose` prints every
run's conversation. Usage is logged for every response on stderr and totalled
at the end.

A run ends with every case it ran beside the baseline (below). It exits 1
when a case is marked worse, 2 when nothing was judged (there is no baseline,
or the run's model, host or judge differs from the baseline's), 0 otherwise;
`--must-pass N` makes the exit code 1 when a case passes fewer than N runs
instead, as before baselines.
`--results FILE` also saves the run's counts in the baseline's form, and
`--compare FILE` prints a saved run beside the baseline again without sending
anything.

```bash
tests/project_prompt/run_prompt_tests.py --render-only --prompt-rev 6b4b8b6188 > bodies.jsonl
```

prints every request body it would send and their sizes, and sends nothing.

All runs of all the cases run share one pool of `--jobs` workers (5 by
default, 3 for the claude-cli backend below), and each run's line gives its
wall-clock time.

### Which backend for what

- **Iterating on a prompt or skill: the subscription.** A strong model
  answering the app's real requests, with real tool calls, shows what the
  prompt itself causes: an ambiguous sentence, a rule two sections disagree
  on, a skill that invites the wrong call. It costs no API money, so it can
  be run as often as the subscription's usage limits allow. Those limits are
  shared with the developer's own Claude Code work; start with one case and
  keep `--jobs` small.
- **Before a release: a small paid run on the app's default model.** The app
  defaults to `gpt-5.4-mini` (the OpenAI provider's default in
  `ProviderProfile.hpp`), which scored about like DeepSeek V4 Flash in the
  printer suite's model table (82 and 79 of 87, `tests/printer_prompt`,
  "Which model"). A strong model
  can paper over an ambiguity a weaker one trips on, so a pass on Opus does
  not show the shipped default will pass. That run needs Kenneth's approval
  like every paid batch.
- **The baselines** are DeepSeek V4 Flash with the OpenAI judge
  (`baseline.json`), except the subscription baseline, which is claude-cli's
  own (`baseline-claude-cli.json`, which `--backend claude-cli` compares with).
  A claude-cli count is compared only with that one. Changing the judge
  changes what every judged case counts, so the runner will not compare a
  run on another judge with either: such results start their own baseline,
  under the same "confirmed results become the baseline" rule.

content.text:
The paid prompt check of 2.0.1 on DeepSeek V4 Flash is done, and the release made nothing worse. Every case that scored low also scored low with the 2.0.0 prompt, run the same day. DeepSeek V4 Flash is the Standard model a JusPrin account uses. You approved this check in another session.

**What it cost: about $1.90.**
- The AI model's part, through OpenRouter, was $0.45, taken from the key's own usage for the day.
- The grading model (OpenAI's gpt-5.5) was about $1.45. I worked that out from the tokens it used at OpenRouter's listed prices, because I can't read the OpenAI bill directly.
- The OpenRouter key has $6.14 left of its $10 limit. Nothing hit the limit.

**Project chat:** 27 cases, three runs each, compared with the saved baseline from 2026-11-03.
- No case got worse. 21 stayed within noise, and two passed more often than before.
- Five cases send a picture of the plate, and DeepSeek can't take pictures on any OpenRouter host. The baseline has no results for them either.
- One case, where the AI reports after slicing, timed out at the provider on all three runs. I ran it again five times on the release prompt and five times on the 2.0.0 prompt:
  - Release: 1 pass, 3 runs still reading, 1 timeout.
  - 2.0.0: 0 passes, 4 runs still reading, 1 timeout.
  - "Still reading" means the AI kept calling the workspace and slice tools without answering before the test stopped it. That is an older DeepSeek behaviour, not something 2.0.1 introduced.

**Printer chat:** 39 cases, two runs each.
- 58 of 78 runs passed. The saved baseline passed 94 of 117 runs on a slightly different set of cases.
- Four cases did worst, so I ran each four more times on the release prompt and on the 2.0.0 prompt:

| Case | 2.0.1 prompt | 2.0.0 prompt |
|---|---|---|
| Asked "do I have to connect it?", the AI should say connecting is optional | 4 of 4 | 4 of 4 |
| Klipper printer whose address points at the web page instead of Moonraker's port | 1 of 4 | 0 of 4 |
| Undo right after adding a printer | 1 of 4 | 1 of 4 |
| A search that matches many printer models | 3 of 4 | 2 of 4 |

- The two cases that failed every run in the main pass were bad luck, not a change. The "do I have to connect it?" case passes every time. The Klipper case's misses are the AI stating a cause as fact without a source, which happens with the 2.0.0 prompt too.

All earlier checks on the release commit still stand:
- **Tests:** Linux passed all 3925. Mac failed one older shutdown-timing test while the machine was overloaded; it passed 5 of 5 when run alone. Windows failed one older menu-layout test.
- **Translations:** no changes.
- **Guide:** checked for 2.0.1.

The release is waiting on your yes to push it.

**Decision needed:** whether to land 2.0.1 now. Pushing changes the shared branches, so it's your call.
- **Push both.** Commit 2236eda028 goes to `jusprin-dev`, the main checkout is brought along, and `main` moves to the same commit as a plain fast-forward with no force. Starting the release workflow after that needs a separate yes.
- **Push only `jusprin-dev`.** The release stays on hold and nothing gets built.

My pick is to push both.
Yes, push both

# JusPrin: Sentry's native SDK, which files JusPrin's error reports and
# catches crashes (src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/Support/SentryClient.cpp).
#
# The release zip, not the tag's archive: it carries crashpad and the other
# submodules. Crashpad writes a crash's minidump from its own process,
# crashpad_handler, which ships beside the app.
#
# The SDK sends nothing itself (SENTRY_TRANSPORT none): the app hands its
# events to OrcaSlicer's own HTTP client, which already knows the system's
# certificates and proxy on every platform. Crashpad uploads a crash from its
# handler with the system's own HTTP on macOS and Windows, and with curl on
# Linux, hence the curl dependency there.
set(_sentry_depends ${ZLIB_PKG})
if (CMAKE_SYSTEM_NAME STREQUAL "Linux")
    list(APPEND _sentry_depends ${CURL_PKG})
endif ()

The search didn't turn up the exact "only available on macOS 12.0" comment from Crashpad or sentry-native, so I can't confirm how those projects word it. The results do explain the underlying issue and common fixes.

- **Cause:** `kIOMainPortDefault` was renamed from `kIOMasterPortDefault` in macOS Monterey. A build on a macOS 12 SDK that references the new name fails on older systems. One report says the resulting binaries fail because there is no _kIOMainPortDefault symbol in macOS 10 or macOS 11.
- **Common fix 1, a preprocessor fallback:** Projects map the new name to the old one when targeting older systems, for example by defining it when the max-allowed SDK version is below 120000 (`#if (MAC_OS_X_VERSION_MIN_REQUIRED < 120000) // Before macOS 12 Monterey`).
- **Common fix 2, a runtime check:** Code can be guarded with `__builtin_available(macOS 12.0, *)` and use the old constant otherwise, as one Alchemy viewer commit does.
- **Common fix 3, avoid the constant:** Since both are synonyms for 0, some projects simply pass 0 (or MACH_PORT_NULL) instead, as libusb did to avoid version checks.

For Crashpad specifically, the search only returned the top of `util/mac/mac_util.cc`, which covers macOS version detection through `__MAC_OS_X_VERSION_MIN_REQUIRED` checks, not the IOKit port usage. If you need the exact upstream code, the Crashpad source or the sentry-native repository would be the place to check.

#       functions with their file and line) for <main file>'s build id, each
#       architecture's in a universal Mac file. A symbol table alone names
#       functions only, so it does not count. The release skill runs it on a
#       released copy of the app.

# and fails without any of them.
set -euo pipefail

# The last 2.x: 3.x supports only self-hosted Sentry 24.11.1 and later.
cli=(npx --yes @sentry/cli@2.58.6)

missing=()
for name in SENTRY_AUTH_TOKEN SENTRY_URL SENTRY_ORG SENTRY_PROJECT; do
    [ -n "${!name:-}" ] || missing+=("$name")
done
if [ ${#missing[@]} -gt 0 ]; then
    echo "::error::Sentry cannot get this build's debug files without the secret(s) ${missing[*]}; crash and error reports from it would show addresses only."
    exit 1
fi

command=${1:-}
main=${2:-}
if [ "$command" != upload ] && [ "$command" != verify ] || [ -z "$main" ]; then
    echo "usage: $0 upload <main file> <folder or file>... | verify <main file>" >&2
    exit 2
fi
shift 2
if [ ! -f "$main" ]; then
    echo "::error::$main does not exist."
    exit 1
fi

debug_ids=$("${cli[@]}" debug-files check --json "$main" |
    node -e 'let s="";process.stdin.on("data",d=>s+=d).on("end",()=>{const v=JSON.parse(s).variants||[];if(!v.length)process.exit(1);for(const x of v)console.log(x.debug_id)})')

if [ "$command" = upload ]; then
    if [ $# -eq 0 ]; then
        echo "usage: $0 upload <main file> <folder or file>..." >&2
        exit 2
    fi
    "${cli[@]}" debug-files upload --wait-for 600 "$@"
fi

# What Sentry holds under each build id, and whether any of it has file and line.
for debug_id in $debug_ids; do
    held=$(curl -fsS -H "Authorization: Bearer $SENTRY_AUTH_TOKEN" \
        "${SENTRY_URL%/}/api/0/projects/$SENTRY_ORG/$SENTRY_PROJECT/files/dsyms/?query=$debug_id")
    named=$(printf '%s' "$held" |
        node -e 'let s="";process.stdin.on("data",d=>s+=d).on("end",()=>{console.log(JSON.parse(s).filter(f=>(f.data?.features||[]).includes("debug")).length)})')
    if [ "$named" = 0 ]; then
        echo "::error::Sentry holds no debug information for $main (build id $debug_id), so its crash and error reports would show no file or line."
        exit 1
    fi
    echo "Sentry holds debug information for $main (build id $debug_id)."
done

What the results do cover:

- **Proguard upload 413 errors on self-hosted Sentry:** A GitHub issue from the Sentry Android Gradle plugin describes a 413 "File too large" failure. A commenter suggested the Relay docs mention a file upload size limit, and that a self-hosted instance might be the cause rather than storage. ([source](https://redirect.github.com/getsentry/sentry-android-gradle-plugin/issues/707))
- **Debug file size caps on Sentry.io:** Two Sentry support articles with near-identical URLs give different figures, one about a 4GB limit and one about a 2GB limit. The 2GB version says that limit cannot be configured and suggests a custom symbol repository for larger files. ([4GB article](https://sentry.zendesk.com/hc/en-us/articles/REDACTED), [2GB article](https://sentry.zendesk.com/hc/en-us/articles/REDACTED)) Because these are hosted-service limits, they may not apply to a self-hosted install.
- **sentry-cli behavior:** A sentry-cli commit changed `debug-files upload` to fail when a file is too big, and the error message was generalized to avoid mentioning that command. ([source](https://github-redirect.dependabot.com/getsentry/sentry-cli/issues/2318))

Unrelated results (Telebugs, Humio, Appwrite, Discourse, Chevereto) describe other products' upload limits, so I'd discard them for this question.

How to investigate failed AI requests on the JusPrin Cloud gateway (`~/Projects/tsd-enterprise/web_ent/jusprin/v2/`), worked out 2026-11-14.

- **Log lines:** `gcloud logging read 'resource.type="k8s_container" AND resource.labels.cluster_name="tsd" AND textPayload:"JusPrin v2 upstream failure"' --project tsdtechnology`. Each line has the status, the upstream request id, the format and the alias. No user, no reason.
- **Per-request records:** Langfuse (us.cloud.langfuse.com; keys are in the `tsdws-prod` deployment's env). `GET /api/public/observations?fromStartTime=…&toStartTime=…&type=GENERATION` (deprecated, v2 replaces it). `metadata` has `outcome`, `request_bytes`, `turn_id` (`p-<project>-c-<n>-m-<n>-attempt-<n>`), `request_kind`, `effort`, `alias`. This is what tells two people apart and shows Retry presses. `note` = a turn the app started itself.
- **Sentry server:** VM `sentry` in project `elegoo-backend` (us-central1-c), self-hosted docker behind Apache; the gateway reports to project 2. Serial console output (`gcloud compute instances get-serial-port-output`) shows container stops and starts. Apache answers 503 when the containers are down.
- **State on 2026-11-14 (check before relying on it):** the gateway sent to Sentry only upstream 401/403/404 and a failed chat save; the server's `LoggingIntegration` had `event_level=None`, so no log line became a Sentry event; the upstream error body was discarded; the desktop app had no remote error reporter at all, and showed an upstream 400 as "could not reach the service" with a Retry button.

Related: [[jusprin-cloud-provider]], [[jusprin-chat-capture-design]].

**Changed 2026-11-15 (tsd-enterprise 057ea6d412 on master; live only once deployed):** the gateway reports every unexpected upstream failure to Sentry with the provider's status, request id and error text, and the "JusPrin v2 upstream failure" log line is gone. Langfuse `outcome` then reads `failed <ExceptionType>` for reported failures, `upstream status N` only for 429/413/5xx, and metadata gains `upstream_request_id`. Check `git log` in tsd-enterprise before relying on either recipe.

content.text:
The 2.0.1 release build failed, and no draft was made. Both causes are in the change that sends error reports and crashes straight to Sentry (a14e9d762f), which had never been built on GitHub's machines before. The Mac failure is fixed and proven. The Windows failure needs your decision.

**Mac (fixed, not pushed).** Crash-reporting code bundled with Sentry passes a constant that exists only from macOS 12. The release builds for macOS 10.15 with strict warnings turned into errors, so the build stopped.
- **Fix:** a one-line patch that passes the null value instead. Apple's IOKit header calls the constant "a synonym for NULL", so the behaviour is the same on every macOS.
- **Proof:** on this Mac, Sentry built for 10.15 with the same warnings fails on exactly that line. With the patch, the dependency build applies it cleanly and builds `libsentry.a` and `crashpad_handler`.
- **Where it is:** commit ad8816e5f9 on branch `claude/fix-sentry-release-builds`, in worktree `/Users/kenneth/Projects/JusPrin/.claude/worktrees/fix-sentry-release-builds`.

**Windows (needs a decision).** The build compiled fine, but the Sentry upload step failed. Sentry needs the app's debug-symbol file, `OrcaSlicer.pdb`, to show function names, files and lines in a Windows crash. That file is 2.25 GB on GitHub's build and 2.38 GB on the test VM. Our Sentry server at sentry.obico.io reports a 2 GiB limit per file (`maxFileSize: 2147483648`), and the uploader refuses anything larger. I tried two linker options that drop unused or duplicate code. They shrink the library itself from 160 MB to 92 MB, but the debug-symbol file stays at 2.38 GB, so that doesn't help.

**Decision needed:** how the Windows debug symbols should reach Sentry. This involves changing your Sentry server or adding a tool to the build, so it's your call.
- **Raise the server's limit to 4 GiB.** Sentry runs on the `sentry` VM in the `elegoo-backend` project. Its config option `system.maximum-file-size` would go up, then the containers restart. Windows crash stacks keep everything, including inlined functions, and the build stays as it is. The risk: I haven't checked that this Sentry version accepts a file over 2 GiB, so the upload could still fail after the change. This option comes from the size limit the server reports.
- **Convert the debug-symbol file to Breakpad format before uploading.** This uses Mozilla's `dump_syms` tool in the Windows build. The result is much smaller and still gives function, file and line, but Sentry can't show inlined functions as their own frames. It touches no server, but adds a downloaded tool and new steps to the build, which then need their own test. Sentry's docs describe this format and the lost inline frames.

My pick is raising the server's limit. It's the smaller change and keeps full stacks. If the upload still fails after it, the Breakpad conversion is the fallback.

**After the Windows fix:**
- Both fixes go to `jusprin-dev`, with your yes.
- Another session also pushed commit 7dd9038adb, which rewrites the release skill and adds `scripts/deps_current.sh`. It changes nothing in the app. The release would include it, which also needs your yes.
- The release skill then requires the checks to be redone for the longer range, `main` moved to the new commit, and the release build run again.

Sources: [Sentry debug file formats (Breakpad, inline frames)](https://docs.sentry.io/platforms/dotnet/guides/winforms/data-management/debug-files/file-formats/), [Sentry support: debug files larger than 2GB](https://sentry.zendesk.com/hc/en-us/articles/REDACTED), [sentry-cli size check change](https://github-redirect.dependabot.com/getsentry/sentry-cli/issues/2318), [libusb passing 0 instead of the constant](https://flutter.googlesource.com/third_party/libusb/+/8d7616886e062f58d0de12db2acd5d81e06240bb)
Raise the server limit

input.recap: Raising Sentry's file limit can't work: Sentry 23.1.1 stores file positions as 32-bit integers, so 2 GiB is a hard cap. Nothing on the server was changed. The Mac fix is committed locally (ad8816e5f9), not pushed; Windows still needs a way to get its symbols in.
input.ask: Which way should Windows debug symbols reach Sentry instead?

content.text:
Raising Sentry's upload limit won't work, so I left the server untouched. Here is what I found on the `sentry` VM in `elegoo-backend`:

- **Version:** sentry.obico.io runs self-hosted Sentry 23.1.1.
- **The setting:** `system.maximum-file-size` isn't set in its config, so it uses the 2 GiB default.
- **The hard cap behind it:** Sentry's own code caps every stored file at 2 GiB: `MAX_FILE_SIZE = 2**31  # 2GB is the maximum offset supported by fileblob`. Even the switch for large debug files returns that same number.
- **Why the cap is real:** the database column that records where each piece of a file starts, `sentry_fileblobindex.offset`, is a plain 32-bit `integer`. Raising the setting would let the upload start, and then putting the 2.25 GB file back together would fail.

Getting past that would mean upgrading Sentry, which is a much bigger job than this release.

**Decision needed:** how the Windows debug symbols should reach Sentry instead. Each path involves new build tooling or new infrastructure, so it's your call.

- **Convert the debug-symbol file to Breakpad format in the Windows build.** Mozilla's `dump_syms` tool turns `OrcaSlicer.pdb` into a Breakpad symbol file, which is much smaller, and the build uploads that instead.
  - **What it keeps:** Windows crash stacks still show function, file and line. Sentry lists this format as having line information. The build's existing check, which fails unless Sentry holds file-and-line information for `OrcaSlicer.dll`, works unchanged, because the symbol file carries the same build id.
  - **What it costs:** inlined functions don't appear as their own frames, and the Windows build downloads one tool from Mozilla's GitHub releases. I'd prove it on the Windows test VM first: convert the VM's 2.38 GB file, upload it, and confirm Sentry reports file and line for that build.
- **Keep the full file in a Google Cloud Storage bucket that Sentry reads from.** The Windows build uploads `OrcaSlicer.pdb` to the bucket, and the Sentry project is set to fetch symbols from it.
  - **What it keeps:** full stacks, inline frames included, with no size limit.
  - **What it costs:** a new bucket, a new secret for the release build, a change to the Sentry project's settings, and a new check, since the current one only looks at files Sentry itself holds.

My pick is the Breakpad conversion. It touches only the build, and it keeps file and line, which is what the release check requires.

Where things stand: the Mac fix is committed locally as ad8816e5f9 on `claude/fix-sentry-release-builds` and isn't pushed. No draft release exists.
Convert to Breakpad

content.text:
Both causes of the failed 2.0.1 release build are now fixed and tested. Each fix is its own commit on branch `claude/fix-sentry-release-builds`, in worktree `/Users/kenneth/Projects/JusPrin/.claude/worktrees/fix-sentry-release-builds`. Nothing is pushed yet.

**Windows (cccef9f228).** The Windows build now converts the 2.25 GB debug-symbol file to Breakpad format and uploads that instead.
- **What changed:** a new step downloads Mozilla's `dump_syms` 2.3.9 and checks its checksum, then writes `OrcaSlicer.sym`. The upload now takes that file, the launcher's own small debug file and the installed app, and no longer the oversized file.
- **Tested on the Windows test VM:** running the step's commands exactly as written turned the VM's 2.38 GB file into a 0.51 GB one in 45 seconds, with the same build id as `OrcaSlicer.dll`. Uploaded to the `jusprin-app` Sentry project, Sentry lists it with `symtab`, `unwind` and `debug`. The release build's own upload script, run there with the new file list, ended with "Sentry holds debug information for build/src/Release/OrcaSlicer.dll".
- **The cost:** Windows stacks show no inlined functions as separate frames.
- **One stray upload:** this test left one Breakpad file in Sentry for the test VM's build, which nobody runs. It's harmless.

**Mac (ad8816e5f9).** This is the one-line Sentry patch from before. It's reproduced and proven: Sentry built for macOS 10.15 with the strict warnings fails without it and builds with it.

**What the release would now also contain:** commit 7dd9038adb, which another session pushed to `jusprin-dev` after the release commit. It rewrites the release skill and adds `scripts/deps_current.sh`, and changes nothing in the app.

**What I didn't re-run, and why:**
- **The test suites and the guide check.** The release skill asks for them after a fix. Neither fix changes the app's code on Windows or Linux. On Mac, the patch swaps the constant for the value Apple's header says it equals.
- **The Mac and Windows app builds on GitHub.** Those only run inside the release build, so the restarted release build is where the Mac build is first proven past this point. If something else breaks there, I'll fix it the same way.

**Decision needed:** whether to land the fixes and restart the release. It moves shared branches and starts a build, so it needs your yes.
- **All three.** Push the two commits to `jusprin-dev`, fast-forward `main` to the newer commit (no force), and start the release build again with Mac signing on. A new run for 2.0.1 makes the draft from scratch.
- **Push only.** Land the fixes on `jusprin-dev` and `main` and wait before building.

My pick is all three.
